### [688d518](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/688d518a8ad65891c5546393eb58f9dca11ec186)

- **作者**: Matthew Bonanni
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T18:58:29Z
- **提交信息**: fix(comm): wait on the cluster barrier before the MNNVL RMSNorm DSMEM exchange (#7782)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## Description

In `LamportFlags::ctaArrive()` (`UseCGA` path,
`include/flashinfer/comm/trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce.cuh`), every thread
arrives at the cluster barrier but only warp 0 of block rank 0 waits.
The RMSNorm cluster reduction that follows
(`oneshotAllreduceFusionKernel`, `rmsNormLamport`) then writes peer
CTAs' shared memory via `cluster.map_shared_rank` with no guarantee
those CTAs are running, and arrives at the barrier again. This breaks
two rules:

- Distributed shared memory may only be accessed once every CTA in the
cluster exists (CUDA Programming Guide: guarantee it with
`cluster.sync()`).
- PTX `barrier.cluster`: "Each thread must arrive at the barrier only
once before the barrier completes."

When the race hits, the kernel dies with Xid 13 `Graphics SM Cga
Exception: CTA Not Present` (`unspecified launch failure`).

This was introduced in #3385, which replaced a full `cluster.sync()`
here with the split arrive/wait.

Fix: every thread waits after arriving (one line moved), restoring the
pre-#3385 synchronization. The arrival-counter update and the non-CGA
path are unchanged.

## Related Issues

- vllm-project/vllm#64327: a TP8 B200 server using this kernel (vLLM's
default single-node fused all-reduce since vllm-project/vllm#61989) with
HiSparse KV offload crashes with `unspecified launch failure` on every
run.
- Blocks vllm-project/vllm#63801 (HiSparse speculative group prefetch):
its extra host-memory gathers make the crash reproducible on H100/H200.
- The [vLLM Mistral Large 4
recipe](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/recipes/models/mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B.yaml)
tells HiSparse users on B200/B300/GB300 to switch to the TRTLLM
all-reduce backend to avoid this crash.

## Tests

Standalone reproducer (script in Reviewer Notes): 4 ranks loop MNNVL
`allreduce_fusion` (`kARResidualRMSNorm`) while a side stream reads
random rows of host memory. flashinfer-python 0.7.2.post1, torch
2.14.0+cu130.

| Config | 4× H200, driver 595.71.05 (VM) | 4× H100, driver 580.126.09 |
|---|---|---|
| MNNVL, side stream on | Xid 13 within seconds | Xid 13 within seconds
|
| MNNVL, two-shot / PDL off / pinned memory | Xid 13 | Xid 13 (two-shot)
|
| MNNVL, side stream off | no crash | no crash |
| MNNVL, side stream reads device memory | no crash | — |
| TRTLLM backend | no crash | — |
| **MNNVL + this PR** | — | **no crash, one-shot and two-shot** |

`compute-sanitizer --tool racecheck` flags the stock kernel even without
the side stream (`Potential invalid __shared__ write ... located in a
block that might not have entered yet`, `oneshotAllreduceFusionKernel`)
and is clean with this PR. On 8× B200 (driver 595.91.07) in a serving
workload with heavy host-memory reads, 7/7 stock runs crashed and none
with this PR.

Fused all-reduce + residual + RMSNorm, bf16, hidden 6144, TP8, CUDA
graph, µs/call (no measurable cost):

| tokens | 1 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 | 64 | 128 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| stock MNNVL | 4.55 | 4.66 | 5.12 | 6.32 | 6.62 | 7.69 | 8.91 |
| MNNVL + this PR | 4.60 | 4.64 | 5.13 | 6.34 | 6.64 | 7.68 | 8.93 |
| TRTLLM | 6.35 | 6.37 | 6.56 | 7.59 | 9.72 | 14.63 | 23.49 |

- [ ] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [ ] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).
- [ ] This PR requires **full-scope** CI, not targeted tests (expensive;
justify below).

Suggested CI test targets: `tests/comm/test_trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce.py
tests/comm/test_trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce_custom_comm.py
tests/comm/test_trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce_dynamic_fp8_quant.py
tests/comm/test_trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce_mxfp8.py`

`pre-commit` passed on the changed file; the FlashInfer unit tests above
were not run locally.

## Reviewer Notes

- No unit test is added: triggering the race takes concurrent
host-memory traffic and many iterations.
- Run the reproducer with `torchrun --nproc-per-node 4 fi_repro.py 120
on` (`off` disables the side stream; env knobs are in the docstring).
The side kernel is built for `sm_90a`.
- `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` and GPU coredump mode both hide the crash.

<details><summary>fi_repro.py</summary>

```python
"""Repro: FlashInfer MNNVL fused allreduce+residual+RMSNorm on the compute
stream while a side stream runs a trivial zero-copy kernel reading random host rows.

torchrun --nproc-per-node 4 fi_repro.py <seconds> <side:on|off>
Env: BACKEND=mnnvl|trtllm, HOSTMEM=register|pinned, SRC=host|device, ONESHOT=1|0, PDL=1|0
"""

import os
import sys
import time

import flashinfer.comm as fc
from flashinfer.comm.comm_backend import TorchDistBackend
import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
from torch.utils.cpp_extension import load_inline

_SRC = r"""
#include <torch/extension.h>
#include <ATen/cuda/CUDAContext.h>
__global__ void zc_gather(const uint4* __restrict__ host, uint4* __restrict__ dst,
                          const int* __restrict__ rows, int n, int vec_per_row) {
  int warp = (blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x) / 32, lane = threadIdx.x % 32;
  int nwarps = gridDim.x * blockDim.x / 32;
  for (int i = warp; i < n; i += nwarps) {
    const uint4* src = host + (long long)rows[i] * vec_per_row;
    uint4* d = dst + (long long)i * vec_per_row;
    for (int j = lane; j < vec_per_row; j += 32) __stcg(d + j, __ldcg(src + j));
  }
}
void launch(int64_t host, torch::Tensor dst, torch::Tensor rows, int64_t row_bytes) {
  zc_gather<<<64, 512, 0, at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream()>>>(
      (const uint4*)host, (uint4*)dst.data_ptr(), rows.data_ptr<int>(), rows.numel(),
      (int)(row_bytes / 16));
}
"""

secs = float(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 300
side_on = (sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "on") == "on"
rank, world = int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"]), int(os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"])
torch.cuda.set_device(rank)
dev = torch.device("cuda", rank)
dist.init_process_group("nccl", device_id=dev)
cpu_group = dist.new_group(backend="gloo")

HIDDEN, MAX_TOK = 6144, 170
ROWS = int(os.environ.get("ROWS", "16"))
oneshot = {"1": True, "0": False}.get(os.environ.get("ONESHOT", ""))
pdl = os.environ.get("PDL", "1") == "1"
ws = fc.create_allreduce_fusion_workspace(
    backend=os.environ.get("BACKEND", "mnnvl"), world_size=world, rank=rank, max_token_num=MAX_TOK,
    hidden_dim=HIDDEN, dtype=torch.bfloat16, comm_backend=TorchDistBackend(group=cpu_group), group=cpu_group,
)
ext = load_inline(
    "zc_gather", cpp_sources="void launch(int64_t, torch::Tensor, torch::Tensor, int64_t);",
    cuda_sources=_SRC, functions=["launch"], extra_cuda_cflags=["-gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=sm_90a"],
)

ROW, NREAD = 656, int(os.environ.get("NREAD", "32768"))
host_rows = int(float(os.environ.get("POOL_GIB", "16")) * 2**30) // ROW
if os.environ.get("SRC", "host") == "device":
    pool = torch.empty(host_rows, ROW, dtype=torch.uint8, device=dev)
elif os.environ.get("HOSTMEM", "register") == "pinned":
    pool = torch.empty(host_rows, ROW, dtype=torch.uint8, pin_memory=True)
else:
    pool = torch.empty(host_rows, ROW, dtype=torch.uint8)
    pool.view(-1)[::4096].zero_()
    assert torch.cuda.cudart().cudaHostRegister(pool.data_ptr(), pool.nbytes, 0).value == 0
dst = torch.empty(NREAD, ROW, dtype=torch.uint8, device=dev)
rows = torch.randint(0, host_rows, (NREAD,), dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)

x = torch.randn(ROWS, HIDDEN, device=dev, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
residual = torch.randn(ROWS, HIDDEN, device=dev, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
gamma = torch.ones(HIDDEN, device=dev, dtype=torch.bfloat16)


def step():
    global residual
    h = x.clone()
    fc.allreduce_fusion(
        input=h, workspace=ws, pattern=fc.AllReduceFusionPattern.kARResidualRMSNorm,
        launch_with_pdl=pdl, residual_out=h, norm_out=torch.empty_like(h), residual_in=residual,
        rms_gamma=gamma, rms_eps=1e-6, use_oneshot=oneshot, fp32_acc=True, layout_code=0, trigger_completion_at_end=False,
    )
    residual = h * 0.5


for _ in range(3):
    step()
ext.launch(pool.data_ptr(), dst, rows, ROW)
torch.cuda.synchronize()
dist.barrier()
if rank == 0:
    print(f"start backend={ws.backend} mc={getattr(ws, 'mc_ptr', None)} oneshot={oneshot} pdl={pdl} side={side_on}", flush=True)
side = torch.cuda.Stream()
t0, n = time.time(), 0
stop = torch.zeros(1, device=dev)
while True:
    if side_on:
        with torch.cuda.stream(side):
            ext.launch(pool.data_ptr(), dst, rows, ROW)
    for _ in range(8):
        step()
    n += 1
    if n % 2000 == 0:
        stop.fill_(float(time.time() - t0 >= secs))
        dist.broadcast(stop, 0)
        if stop.item():
            break
        if rank == 0:
            print(f"iters={n} t={time.time() - t0:.0f}s ok", flush=True)
torch.cuda.synchronize()
if rank == 0:
    print(f"done iters={n} side={side_on}", flush=True)
os._exit(0)
```

</details>

### [1f0821b](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/1f0821b7e343aef0270dccc02efe0154c67af0c3)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T18:55:59Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn_kcp): with grad, reuse recomputed normalized Q/K in the checkpointed backward of the non-deterministic KCP package (#8349)

`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_train_kcp` is the non-deterministic
KCP (key-value context parallel) GDN training package. It supports BF16
in three KCP layouts: contiguous (C), zigzag (Z) and zigzag-per-document
(D). Each can run with or without the in-kernel Q/K L2 norm. The
operations are forward, forward+backward, and checkpointed 2 x forward +
backward with or without a recompute handle, in eager mode or under CUDA
graphs. This host-only PR changes one variant: the checkpointed backward
with the in-kernel Q/K L2 norm. With `use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True` and
kept recompute tapes (`torch.utils.checkpoint`, with or without a
recompute handle), the recompute forward passes its normalized Q/K rows
to the backward, so the backward no longer launches a Q/K
re-normalization kernel (10 -> 9 backward launches) and outputs and
gradients stay bitwise equal to FlashInfer main.

## Speedup vs deterministic Cake and the strongest non-Cake
implementation

**Baselines.** Deterministic Cake is
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_det_train_kcp` at FlashInfer main
04ff9ccf with `use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True`. The strongest non-Cake
implementation is FlashQLA 0.1.3 dual-CP (inter + intra CP). It runs
only the contiguous layout and was timed in a separate run, so its
contiguous-layout times are also the reference for the D and Z rows. It
is the fastest qualified non-Cake arm in every row. FLA 0.6.0 KCP and
head-parallel all-to-all around FLA / cuDNN frontend 1.32.1 `gdn_frost`
were also measured. The recompute-handle operation exists only in Cake,
so its non-Cake cells are n/a.

**Operations.** bwd = fwd+bwd - fwd, derived from the medians. ckpt =
`torch.utils.checkpoint`, 2 x forward + backward. ckpt + recompute
handle = the same with one recompute handle per step.

Speedup = baseline ms / this PR ms, computed from the 3-decimal
absolutes shown. A ratio below 1.000 is marked "non-Cake faster" or
"non-det slower" (this PR's package is the non-deterministic one).

### NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a)

NVIDIA B200, sm_100a, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.1. Workload K3E: CP8,
documents 98304/65536/57344/40960 tokens, T/rank 32768, heads (16, 48),
BF16, causal conv1d on, `use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True` on every arm.
Timing: slowest rank, median CUDA-event time, palindromic arm order,
eager. No cell reached the 5 % software power-cap threshold.

| GPU / arch | workload | operation | deterministic Cake ms | strongest
non-Cake ms (arm) | this PR ms | speedup vs deterministic Cake | speedup
vs non-Cake |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a) | K3E CP8 C | fwd | 2.746 | 2.445 (FlashQLA
dual-CP, C) | 2.724 | 1.008 | 0.898 (non-Cake faster; separate run) |
| NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a) | K3E CP8 C | bwd (= fwd+bwd - fwd) | 4.608 |
7.207 (FlashQLA dual-CP, C) | 4.584 | 1.005 | 1.572 (separate run) |
| NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a) | K3E CP8 C | fwd+bwd | 7.354 | 9.652 (FlashQLA
dual-CP, C) | 7.308 | 1.006 | 1.321 (separate run) |
| NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a) | K3E CP8 C | ckpt (2 x fwd + bwd) | 8.305 |
12.045 (FlashQLA dual-CP, C) | 8.262 | 1.005 | 1.458 (separate run) |
| NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a) | K3E CP8 C | ckpt + recompute handle (Cake

### [536b44e](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/536b44e1855d471bb7ec2c066ba8f8bc38c66902)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T18:55:41Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_msa_icp_indexer): faster list publisher and early merge trigger on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a (#8358)

The MiniMax-M3 index-context-parallel (ICP) sparse-attention indexer
(`flashinfer.msa_ops` `msa_icp_*`) has two decode chains. The default
chain is score plane + select publish. The fused chain is list scorer +
list publisher (`msa_icp_decode_score_publish`). On every layout, decode
ends with a candidate merge that combines the publishers' per-rank top-k
candidate lists into the final top-k. The merge has three records:
merge, merge_legacy for the legacy receive rows, and merge_prefill. This
PR changes two kernels: the list publisher in the fused chain and the
tagged candidate merge.

Both changes apply on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a. The list publisher
now reads each candidate list with 16-byte loads straight into the
running top 16. It runs a merge-network level only while the split count
still needs one. The publisher now requires an even pool row stride. The
package already checks that a caller pool is contiguous uint8, 16-byte
aligned and a whole number of 8-byte rows. The tagged candidate merge
now triggers the dependent launch at entry for every world size, where
before it did so only for two ranks. The sparse attention kernel that
follows therefore launches and runs its prologue while the merge
finishes, and it waits on the grid dependency before it reads the merge
output. Outputs are bit-identical. The decode scorers, select publish
and the prefill merge are unchanged, and legacy merge behaviour is
unchanged. Speedup against the previous version in FlashInfer main:

| World | Page | Cohort | Previous (ms) | New (ms) | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TP4 | P128 | steady | 9.306 | 9.155 | 1.016x |
| TP4 | P128 | mixed | 9.723 | 9.604 | 1.012x |
| TP2 | P128 | steady | 14.317 | 14.273 | 1.003x |
| TP2 | P128 | mixed | 14.807 | 14.745 | 1.004x |
| TP4 | P256 | steady | 9.218 | 9.170 | 1.005x |
| TP4 | P256 | mixed | 9.622 | 9.556 | 1.007x |

*NVIDIA VR200 (sm_107a), 4 GPUs per node, CUDA 13.4. Workload:
MiniMax-M3 serving, 163840 input tokens, 8192 output tokens, 14
concurrent requests. Steady: the 14 requests decode together. Mixed: the
same 14 requests, plus one extra request whose chunked prefill runs in
mixed batches with the 14 decodes. Values are the median GPU time of a
decode step. n = 4 rounds, and each round runs previous and new back to
back on one node. Speedup = previous / new.*

End-to-end output throughput (tok/s), same runs. Ratio = new / previous,
taken as the median of the per-round pair ratios.

| World | Page | Steady: previous -> new (ratio) | Mixed: previous ->
new (ratio) |
|---|---|---|---|
| TP4 | P128 | 2053.2 -> 2073.8 (1.010) | 1958.1 -> 1964.0 (1.003) |
| TP2 | P128 | 1500.2 -> 1502.9 (1.002) | 1484.2 -> 1487.5 (1.002) |
| TP4 | P256 | 2060.3 -> 2066.0 (1.001) | 1977.7 -> 1985.2 (1.004) |

| World | Page | Cohort | Previous (us) | New (us) | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TP4 | P128 | steady | 12570.7 | 12433.5 | 1.011x |

*NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a), CUDA 13.4. Same workload and steady cohort as
above. On this layout GB300 runs the default score plane + select
publish chain, so the tagged candidate merge is the only change from
this PR that runs here. Values are the median over rounds of the decode
step span measured by the profiler. n = 8 rounds, and each round runs
previous and new back to back on one node. Speedup = previous / new of
the medians. The median per-round ratio new / previous is 0.991, with a
range of 0.976 to 1.014 and 1 of 8 rounds above 1. The per-round spread
is larger than the effect, so on GB300 this is parity (no regression),
not a measured speedup. B200 (sm_100a) was not timed end to end.*

The indexer ships the prefill path, the tagged and legacy receive rows,
and the P128/P256 x TP2/TP4 decode layouts on sm_100a (B200), sm_103a
(GB300) and sm_107a (VR200), and this PR changes the list publisher and
the tagged candidate merge on all three architectures and leaves the
scorers, select publish and prefill kernels unchanged.

### [4386625](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/43866254682064edbcec24657657363290d165d3)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T18:50:29Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mxfp8_megamoe_ep16): 104-cluster schedule for the sm_107a CuTe-DSL backend (#8330)

`cake_mxfp8_megamoe_ep16` is a fused MegaMoE forward kernel with BF16
activations and MXFP8 weights. It runs with expert parallelism over 16
ranks (EP16), with H3072, I5120, 512 experts and top-8 routing. It has
two backends: CUDA, the default, and CuTe-DSL. This PR changes only the
CuTe-DSL backend on sm_107a (Rubin R200). The two sm_107a CuTe-DSL fused
programs now use the schedule that the CUDA backend already uses on
sm_107a. The persistent grid grows from 144 CTAs (72 two-CTA clusters)
to 208 CTAs (104 clusters), and work splits into the same two uneven
classes: 32 clusters take 13 FC1 + 3 FC2 items (432 weight K tiles) and
72 clusters take 12 FC1 + 4 FC2 items (448 K tiles). Each item still
accumulates over the whole K, so outputs are bitwise identical to the
previous version and to the CUDA backend. Compared with the previous
Cake version of this kernel (the 144-CTA sm_107a CuTe-DSL programs), the
new build is 1.23-1.25x faster. Compared with FlashInfer's native
`MoEEpMegaLayer` (BF16 x MXFP8), tuned to the fastest of 18
configurations per row, it is 1.64-1.68x faster.

EP16 on 4 nodes x 4 NVIDIA R200 (sm_107a, 212 SMs), CUDA 13.0, PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130; eager mode, cold L2, CUDA events. In each round, the
reported value is the slowest of the 16 ranks, using each rank's median
over 40 iterations. Each table value is the median over 16 rounds.
`balanced` = uniform expert load; `hotset50` = 50% of routes go to a hot
subset of experts.

| tokens/rank | routing | previous (us) | new (us) | speedup vs previous
| native tuned (us) | speedup vs native |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16 | balanced | 246.59 | 196.82 | 1.25x | 330.59 | 1.68x |
| 16 | hotset50 | 250.79 | 203.44 | 1.23x | 333.32 | 1.64x |
| 32 | balanced | 247.83 | 201.22 | 1.23x | 330.61 | 1.64x |
| 32 | hotset50 | 249.06 | 202.03 | 1.23x | 331.95 | 1.64x |
| 64 | balanced | 252.49 | 203.18 | 1.24x | 332.99 | 1.64x |
| 64 | hotset50 | 251.76 | 203.06 | 1.24x | 334.89 | 1.65x |

Both the CUDA and CuTe-DSL backends ship for sm_100a, sm_103a and
sm_107a, and the module supports EP16 only. This change affects only the
sm_107a CuTe-DSL build.

### [8a645b6](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/8a645b6a5780fc3e8a8e32e8e6642b6ed1706403)

- **作者**: danisereb
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T18:48:22Z
- **提交信息**: feat(moe): support ClampedRelu2 in the CuTe-DSL fused MoE (#7286)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Builds on #6793 (CuTe-DSL MXFP8 x MXFP8 MoE, now merged). 

Adds support for the existing `ActivationType.ClampedRelu2` (added for
the CUTLASS fused MoE in #5696) to the CuTe-DSL block-scaled fused MoE,
with the same API and math as the CUTLASS implementation:
a non-gated bounded ReLU^2, `(L * tanh(relu(x) / L)) ** 2`, where `x` is
the alpha-scaled FC1 accumulator and `L` is a model-wide clamp scale. It
is fused into the gather GEMM1 epilogue (vectorized and scalar
paths).

**Changes**
- `ActivationType.ClampedRelu2` on the SM100 block-scaled path: MXFP8 x
MXFP8, NVFP4 x NVFP4 and MXFP4 x MXFP8, which
share the GEMM1 kernel. W4A16, the SM90 path and SM107 reject it with an
explicit error (local allow-lists; the
  activation normalizer is unchanged).
- `clamped_relu2_limit`: a `(1,)` float32 tensor on the input's device,
accepted by `cute_dsl_fused_moe`,
`CuteDslMoEWrapper` and the GEMM1 entry points. Validation mirrors
`cutlass_fused_moe` (same checks and error text):
required with `ClampedRelu2`, rejected with any other activation, no
host-side value check and no device sync.
- Kernel: the limit is read from device memory once per CTA (after the
PDL wait) and `1 / L` is computed on device, so
one compiled kernel serves any limit and in-place updates are picked up
at the next launch (CUDA-graph friendly). The
limit value is not part of any kernel or autotuner cache key. `Relu2`
code generation is unchanged.
- Existing activations keep their behaviour, tactics and cache keys.

## 🔍 Related Issues

- Builds on #6793 (CuTe-DSL MXFP8 x MXFP8 MoE), merged.
- #5696 (ClampedRelu2 for the CUTLASS fused MoE): same activation and
API.

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

On GB200 (SM100):
- `pytest tests/moe/test_cute_dsl_mxfp8_moe.py`: MXFP8 accuracy against
a clamped reference for two limits x two GEMM1
tactics, a check that the clamp is active (the output differs from plain
ReLU^2), runtime limit read (in-place update,
  same compiled kernel), argument validation. 16 passed.
- `pytest tests/moe/test_cute_dsl_fused_moe.py`: NVFP4 accuracy against
a clamped reference (per-tensor and per-token
activation scales), argument validation, the limit value staying out of
the cache key, ClampedRelu2 rejection on
  W4A16. 716 passed, 16 skipped.
- SM90 rejection is covered in `tests/moe/test_cute_dsl_bf16_moe.py` and

can switch MoE backends without changing how they pass the limit.
- The limit is a runtime tensor rather than a compile-time constant on
purpose: one compiled kernel per activation type, no recompilation or
cache-key growth per model.

### [a101601](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/a101601c82aacea4536ece72eeb507a95109cb13)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T18:33:02Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_kda): with grad, follow the deterministic block-table and fence re-render in the non-deterministic package [stacked on #8328] (#8347)

The deterministic package's records table_v3, seg_table and fwd_intra_v14 now
build the v4 block-table writers: every document of at least 4 P chunks ends
in a short segment of the uniform block table. Its fused gradients also take a
shared-memory proxy fence before the hd_empty and hd_read_done arrives. The
non-deterministic package copies these programs.

- The three carried copies take the new programs' names and units, and the
  four fenced fused-gradient copies take the new units.
- The hand-off twin of the record fwd_intra_v14 is rebuilt from the new
  forward intra kernel, so the checkpoint recompute writes the same block
  tables as the forward. The record name fwd_intra_v19 and HANDOFF_TWINS do
  not change.
- The S1 fused gradient takes the same fence before its hd_read_done arrive.
  Its program names do not change, and the fence changes no output value.

### [7c395b6](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/7c395b6e81227b2d464a08cdddcaff416384bb29)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T18:30:25Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_dsa_indexer_det): ack the verdict word before the next unit stores it (#8355)

`flashinfer.dsa_indexer.dsa_indexer_det_topk` is the Cake deterministic
DSA indexer top-k scan. It ships in the package
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_dsa_indexer_det`. It uses BF16 queries and
keys, and FP32 head weights and scores. It returns the top-k key ids for
each query. The ids and scores do not depend on partition or chunking.
Ties go to the larger id. Cake ships one variant of this kernel. This PR
fixes a race in the kernel. Each CTA draws units of work. For each unit,
the math warps store a verdict word in shared memory. The verdict word
says whether the unit has key tiles and whether its threshold pass
failed. The fail flags are shared fail flags. In the CTA-pair programs,
they are pair fail flags. The K-loader warp and the MMA warp read the
verdict word. The gate-warpgroup programs are not affected. In every
other program, nothing stopped the math warps from storing the next
unit's verdict word and fail flags too early. They could store them
before the K loader and the MMA warp had read the current ones. This can
happen when the next unit has no key tiles. The two readers could then
read overwritten values. The phase parity of the verdict barrier could
also alias, which can in principle hang. We never saw wrong outputs, and
we never saw the hang. This is a correctness fix. Times do not change
beyond run-to-run noise.

- It adds a `verdict_ack` mbarrier with an arrival count of 2.
- The K loader and one thread of the MMA warp arrive on `verdict_ack`
after they read the verdict word.
- The Q-loader warp waits on `verdict_ack` before it signals that the
next unit's Q tile is ready (`q_full`). The math warps store the next
verdict word only after `q_full`. So they store it only after both
reads.
- On sm_100a and sm_103a, the Q loader waits before it issues the next Q
tile load. On sm_107a, it issues the load first and waits before its
`q_full` arrive. This hides the wait behind the load.
- The gate-warpgroup programs already had an acknowledgement. They do
not change.
- Program choice does not change on any GPU. Only the compiled kernels
of the affected programs change.

| GB200 (sm_100a) | 0.985x | 0.999x | 1.023x |
| sm_107a | 0.992x | 1.000x | 1.007x |

The baseline is the previous Cake version on FlashInfer main, speedup is

### [8bb3a3f](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/8bb3a3fe0d47cb7bf6fbd7c18be68d507c10e3eb)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T18:29:33Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kda_det): short block-table segments under side-stream contention, dqkg smem fence (#7548) (#8328)

## Summary

The deterministic Cake KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) chunked training
kernels (`flashinfer.cake_kda_det_train`: `chunk_kda_det`,
`chunk_kda_det_fwd`, `chunk_kda_det_bwd`) ship these variants:

- Gate form: preactivated `g` (FP32, default) or raw gate
(`use_gate_in_kernel=True`, BF16 raw gate with `A_log` / `dt_bias` /
`lower_bound`).
- Training path: non-checkpointed (the forward saves the saved set and
the backward reads it) or checkpointed (`chunk_kda_det_bwd` without
`saved` replays the forward).
- Package: single-rank `cake_kda_det_train` or context-parallel
`cake_kda_det_train_kcp`.

This PR changes only the single-rank package. It addresses the KDA part
of #7548, where the KDA backward slows down while another kernel is
resident on a side stream. It makes two changes:

- The block-table writers and the intra-chunk forward kernels (g and raw
gate) now end each long document with one short block-table segment and
split the rest evenly over the other segments. A kernel resident on
another stream now slows KDA in proportion to the SMs that it occupies.
- The six dqkg kernels get the missing async-proxy shared-memory fence.

Baseline: the previous Cake version, which is FlashInfer main
`0dbfeafe08cdd75dfa1382c5b6f8009fc5ec3721`. The deterministic package
was last changed there by #8276.

CUDA 13.4, torch 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA 13.0 runtime).** Both versions run
in the same process and alternate on every iteration. Timing uses CUDA
events around one call, with 10 warmup iterations and 120 pairs per row.
"Speedup main / PR" is the median of the per-pair ratios, so it can
differ from main ms / PR ms. **A speedup below 1 means this PR is
slower.** On B200, 30 of 32 rows are slightly slower; the lowest speedup
is 0.9906.

## Side-stream contention (#7548 shape)

**Table 3: NVIDIA GB200, sm_100a, 152 SMs. CUDA: nvcc 13.4.92, driver
CUDA 13.4, torch 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA 13.0 runtime).** Shape: S=261393, 4
docs (120001/70707/65537/5148), H=4, gate `g`. The side kernel starts on
its own stream and spins or sleeps for 80M cycles. Then the main stream
sleeps for 2M cycles, and then the timed call runs. Each arm has 104
samples (4 rounds x 26 reps). "x / alone" is the median under the side
kernel divided by the same arm's median with no side kernel. "bound
1+k/SMs" is the expected proportional slowdown when the side kernel
occupies k SMs. **In the speedup column, a value below 1 means this PR
is slower.** With a 1-SM side kernel, the main bwd slows by 1.0168 and
1.0162, which is above the bound of 1.0066. With this PR, the bwd slows
by 1.0032. This PR is slower in the bwd rows with no side kernel
(speedup 0.9959) and with the 16-CTA side kernel (0.9928).

| op | side kernel | k SMs | main ms | PR ms | speedup main / PR | main
/ alone | PR / alone | bound 1+k/SMs |

| fwd | none (alone) | 0 | 1.4004 | 1.3964 | 1.0022 | 1.0000 | 1.0000 |
1.0000 |
| fwd | t1 (1 CTA x 1 thread, `torch.cuda._sleep`) | 1 | 1.4066 | 1.4045
| 1.0015 | 1.0044 | 1.0058 | 1.0066 |
| fwd | c1x128 (1 CTA x 128 threads spin) | 1 | 1.4066 | 1.4025 | 1.0022
| 1.0044 | 1.0044 | 1.0066 |
| fwd | c16x640 (16 CTAs x 640 threads spin) | 16 | 1.5141 | 1.5110 |
1.0020 | 1.0812 | 1.0821 | 1.1053 |
| fwd | c32x640 (32 CTAs x 640 threads spin) | 32 | 1.6708 | 1.6708 |
1.0000 | 1.1930 | 1.1965 | 1.2105 |
| bwd | none (alone) | 0 | 3.2293 | 3.2426 | 0.9959 | 1.0000 | 1.0000 |
1.0000 |
| bwd | t1 (1 CTA x 1 thread, `torch.cuda._sleep`) | 1 | 3.2836 | 3.2529
| 1.0091 | 1.0168 (above bound) | 1.0032 | 1.0066 |
| bwd | c1x128 (1 CTA x 128 threads spin) | 1 | 3.2815 | 3.2529 | 1.0085
| 1.0162 (above bound) | 1.0032 | 1.0066 |

1.0022 | 1.1723 | 1.1655 | 1.2105 |

This PR does not change the other Cake variants: the context-parallel
deterministic package `cake_kda_det_train_kcp` (g and raw gate) and the
non-deterministic `cake_kda_train` (which changes separately in stacked
PR #8347). The family builds for sm_100a (B200 / GB200), sm_103a (B300 /
GB300) and sm_107a (R200), but these timings were measured only on
sm_100a.

### [80bb231](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/80bb2313018736f6581fa6289e3bd9b9e536b2d7)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T18:22:11Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_alpha_moe): NVFP4 one-token up merges its K splits in a cluster on sm_100a (#8353)

AlphaMoE has three Cake kernel sets in FlashInfer: NVFP4 MoE (FP4
activations and weights, BF16 output), W8A8 MoE (FP8 block-scaled
activations and weights, BF16 output), and the fused 512-expert router.
This PR changes only NVFP4 MoE. W8A8 MoE and the router are unchanged.
In NVFP4 MoE, the one-token decode path (M = 1) on sm_100a (B200) now
uses the cluster-merge build of its split-K up kernel, which sm_103a
(GB300) has run since #8283. The four K splits of a token form a (1, 1,
4) cluster and merge their FP32 partial sums in one CTA's shared memory,
in the same order, instead of through a global workspace and merge
counters. The workspace-merge build is removed, so one route-1 up kernel
serves both architectures, and outputs are bitwise identical. Against
the previous Cake version of this kernel on FlashInfer main (from
#8283), the touched M=1 shape is 1.077x faster (19.74 us before, 18.33
us now). The two M=8 rows are controls that do not use the M = 1 path.
They run the same kernels as before and show 1.000x and 0.999x.

Kernel time per call in microseconds (sum of the MoE kernels of one
call), cold L2 (memset flush), mean of 4 medians (2 nodes x 2 GPUs);
CUDA 13.3; B200 (sm_100a).

#### B200 (sm_100a)

| MoE | Shape | previous (us) | this PR (us) | speedup |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| NVFP4 | M=1, N=1024, K=6144, E=256, top_k=8, block_m=8 | 19.74 | 18.33
| 1.077x |
| NVFP4 | M=8, N=1024, K=6144, E=256, top_k=8, block_m=8 | 70.17 | 70.15
| 1.000x |
| NVFP4 | M=8, N=256, K=7168, E=256, top_k=8, block_m=8 | 32.30 | 32.31
| 0.999x |

These AlphaMoE kernels ship for sm_100a (B200) and sm_103a (GB300), and
this PR leaves GB300 (sm_103a) device code and timing unchanged; the
other Cake variants are the existing NVFP4 routes (the other batch-size
paths), the W8A8 routes (quad, pair, deep-ring pair, L2-prefetch pair),
and the fused router configurations already on FlashInfer main.

### [b84db04](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/b84db0451de34fbb4e06bab3b8e57628001e2c3d)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T18:21:43Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kda): BF16 KDA prefill sm_103a scalar-beta map fold keeps the gathered epilogue spill-free (#8352)

The Cake chunked KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) prefill behind
`flashinfer.recurrent_kda(..., backend="cake")` has 85 modules: 51 with
BF16 inputs and 34 with TF32 inputs. They come in fused and split forms.
This PR changes only the prepared BF16-input path with FP32 state
(`flashinfer.prepare_bf16_kda_prefill`). It targets split-form launches
on the chain route, and only on sm_103a (GB300). One generated program
changes: the chain-route map-fold main kernel for scalar (per-head) beta
with gate lower bound -5. Before this PR, that kernel's epilogue warps
on the gathered-index path held each window's checkpoint row start
across their whole chunk loop. That made the compiler spill a register
and recompute the thread index inside the loop. Now the warps keep only
the window's row-table entry. They compute the row start at each
checkpoint row they store. The spill is gone. Outputs are bit-identical.
The PR also re-renders 6 split-scan programs from the current Cake
sources. That is a small expression rewrite: the look-ahead map fill
states its slot inline. Fused-kernel program names now also carry a new
build option, with unchanged program text. The tables compare this PR
against the previous Cake version on FlashInfer main. They report median
latency per call in microseconds, with a cold L2. Each table has 56
rows: 12 or 16 heads, no gate lower bound or -5, and 14 sequence-length
shapes. TIE means no difference beyond the measurement band. A repeat on
a second GPU node confirmed every faster row. The split-scan re-render
ran on all split-route rows and measured TIE. B200 runs no changed
program except the re-rendered split scans. On B200, all 56 rows TIE in
both tables, at 1.00x. The first table shows repeated calls on the same
buffers, which use the plan-cache fast path. On GB300, 4 rows are faster
and 52 TIE, with ratios from 1.00x to 1.02x. All four faster rows have
12 heads and gate lower bound -5. At 8192 and 32768 tokens, latency
drops from 142.94 to 141.73 us and from 414.80 to 411.18 us. At
3000+13384 and 2x(8128+64), it drops from 247.71 to 243.81 us (1.02x)
and from 233.12 to 230.86 us. The second table shows the serving
pattern, where every call rebinds the cached plan to new buffers. On
GB300, 3 rows are faster and 53 TIE, with ratios from 1.00x to 1.01x.
The faster rows again have 12 heads and gate lower bound -5. At 16384,
32768 and 3000+13384 tokens, latency drops from 236.78 to 234.56, 416.98
to 411.89 and 247.20 to 243.73 us. Each of these gains is under 2
percent.

B200: NVIDIA B200, sm_100a, 148 SMs, driver 580.82.07. GB300: NVIDIA
GB300, sm_103a, 152 SMs, driver 580.159.03. CUDA 13.4 (nvcc), PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130.

### [7b9de01](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/7b9de01a91b4aae1befe9473ac6ffb1dcb32b223)

- **作者**: Nhat Minh
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T18:20:21Z
- **提交信息**: perf(quantization): add register-resident CUDA backend (#5546)

## 📌 Description

Add an explicit `backend="cuda"` for `per_token_group_quant_8bit` when
`group_size=128`.

The native CUDA kernel assigns one 16-lane half warp to each
quantization group. Each lane keeps eight FP16/BF16 values in registers,
participates in a half-warp absmax reduction, and writes eight FP8/INT8
values with vectorized I/O. This removes the shared-memory round trip
and block-wide synchronization from the group reduction path.

The backend supports:

- FP16 and BF16 input; FP8 E4M3, FP8 E5M2, and INT8 output.
- Row-major and column-major scales, TMA-aligned scale storage, and
UE8M0 scales.
- Unaligned contiguous input through a scalar-load path.
- Empty tensors without launching a zero-sized grid.

`"cutile"` remains the default. Unsupported CUDA configurations raise a
clear error instead of silently falling back to another backend.

### Performance

Environment: H100 and B200, CUDA 13.0.1 FlashInfer CI image.
Measurements use `bench_gpu_time` with 5 dry runs, 30 repeats, cold-L2
mode, and CUDA events because CUPTI was unavailable.

Reproduction:

```bash
python3 benchmarks/bench_per_token_group_quant_8bit.py \
  --providers cuda,cutile --baseline cutile --dst-dtype fp8_e4m3
python3 benchmarks/bench_per_token_group_quant_8bit.py \
  --providers cuda,cutile --baseline cutile --dst-dtype int8
```

Across the benchmark's 33-shape `(num_tokens, hidden_dim)` sweep:

| GPU | Output | Geomean speedup vs cuTile | CUDA faster |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| H100 | FP8 E4M3 | 1.64x | 33/33 shapes |
| H100 | INT8 | 1.74x | 33/33 shapes |
| B200 | FP8 E4M3 | 1.61x | 26/33 shapes |

Representative absolute latencies (CUDA / cuTile):

| GPU | Output | Shape | CUDA | cuTile | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| H100 | FP8 E4M3 | `(128, 4096)` | 0.00658 ms | 0.00819 ms | 1.24x |
| H100 | FP8 E4M3 | `(512, 7168)` | 0.01042 ms | 0.02293 ms | 2.20x |
| H100 | FP8 E4M3 | `(4096, 7168)` | 0.04064 ms | 0.14374 ms | 3.54x |
| H100 | INT8 | `(2048, 7168)` | 0.02320 ms | 0.07496 ms | 3.23x |
| B200 | FP8 E4M3 | `(128, 4096)` | 0.00717 ms | 0.00918 ms | 1.28x |
| B200 | FP8 E4M3 | `(4096, 7168)` | 0.03376 ms | 0.12592 ms | 3.73x |

The B200 path is launch-bound for the smallest inputs; the worst
observed point was 0.99x (`0.00720 ms` CUDA vs `0.00715 ms` cuTile at
`(16, 7168)`).

## 🔍 Related Issues

No FlashInfer issue. The register-resident design was motivated by [vLLM
PR #55330](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55330).

Quantization sources have no CODEOWNERS rule, so they fall through to
the catch-all `*`, whose owners do not include the quantization
maintainer. An approval from that maintainer therefore does not count
toward the required code-owner review (for example on #5546, where all
six changed files match only the catch-all).
This adds a `Quantization` section after `Norm` covering the existing
quantization paths (`flashinfer/quantization/`, the
`fp4_quantization`/`fp8_quantization` shims and JIT specs,
`csrc/quantization.cu`, the FP4 KV quantize/dequantize kernels,
`include/flashinfer/quantization.cuh`, docs, benchmarks and tests), with
the same owner set as the `Norm` section.
Every pattern was checked against the tracked files on current main, and
all six files in #5546 now match a Quantization rule.

- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kimi_k3_attn_res): token-queue and register-carry programs for more GB300 and B200 shapes (#8351)

This PR changes routes of the Cake AttnRes operator,
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_kimi_k3_attn_res`, which is exposed as
`flashinfer.kimi_k3_attn_res.prepare_kimi_k3_attn_res` and
`kimi_k3_attn_res`. One launch does residual add, an optional snapshot
write, K+1 candidate scoring, softmax, mix and output RMSNorm. It takes
BF16 inputs with hidden size 7168 and K in [0, 8]. It has one data type,
one layout and two fused forms: dense and snapshot write. This PR
changes routes on GB300 and B200 at both PDL modes. B300 has no route
change. Among the measured shapes, 27 change on GB300 and 2 on B200, all
of them dense.

- **Token-queue persistent programs (GB300, 152 SMs):** 25 dense shapes
with K 1 to 8 and M 4096 to 16384 move to token-queue (`_clc`) builds of
their current persistent program. A token-queue build launches one CTA
per token (grid M) and uses cluster launch control. Each running CTA
processes its own token and then the tokens of the CTAs it cancels. This
spreads tokens over the SMs dynamically instead of by a static stride.
- **Token-queue persistent programs (B200):** M 4096 K 5 moves to the
new `persistent:k5_nc3_d3_f010000000000000_clc`, and M 12288 K 6 moves
to `persistent:k6_nc4_d2_f110000000000000_clc`.

`persistent:k3_nc2_d2_f111000000000000_fm_rcp`. M 512 K 4 moves from
`persistent:k4_nc3_d3_f110000000000000_fm` to
`persistent:k4_nc3_d2_f111000000000000_fm_rcp`. A packed-register-carry
(`_rcp`) build keeps the running carry in registers instead of tensor
memory.

The program set goes from 212 programs (244 libraries: 112 sm_100a, 132
sm_103a) to 207 programs (239 libraries: 113 sm_100a, 126 sm_103a). This

- **提交信息**: fix(attention): make FA2 paged-prefill stride dispatch portable (#8048)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Native Windows ARM64 nvcc/MSVC rejects FA2 paged-prefill JIT builds with
`"#" not expected here` because stride-mode preprocessor directives
appear inside the `DISPATCH_context` arguments. Replace that selection
with C++17 `if constexpr` and move unsupported-mode rejection to a
file-scope `static_assert`.

Preserve runtime, equal, and independent stride specialization behavior,
including the equal-mode rejection of unequal strides. The change is
limited to `csrc/batch_prefill_paged.cuh`.

## 🔍 Related Issues

[NVBug 7003339](https://nvbugspro.nvidia.com/bug/7003339) (NVIDIA
authentication required).

### [23d065c](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/23d065c54c7d555a93d4a9c17627b439b4249bbf)

- **时间**: 2026-11-02T16:40:26Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mok_bf16): quantize both MXFP8 weight layouts from one read (#7821) (#8346)

`cake_mok_bf16` is FlashInfer's MoK mixture-of-experts training kernel
family, covering forward, checkpoint recompute and backward. It has four
variants: BF16 or MXFP8 routed experts, each with plain or clamped
SwiGLU. This PR delivers the MXFP8 weight quantizer
(`quantize_mok_mxfp8_weights` / `mxfp8_quantize`). After each weight
update, the quantizer converts the routed weights into two layouts:
normal for forward and recompute, and transposed for backward. Each
layout is E4M3 data plus UE8M0 block scales. The previous quantizer on
FlashInfer main used one launch per layout, so it read the BF16 weights
twice. The new one reads each BF16 128x128 tile once and writes both
layouts in a single Triton launch, with byte-identical outputs.

normal + 0.408 transposed) | 0.387 | 1.39x |
| down quantize, both layouts | [36, 4096, 2048] | 0.535 (0.128 normal +
0.407 transposed) | 0.386 | 1.39x |
| `quantize_mok_mxfp8_weights` (gate, up, down) | 3 matrices above |
1.545 | 1.127 | 1.37x |

### [f8f2593](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/f8f2593798ea9a4c981c641fde5e62db197b3335)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T16:38:02Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_gemm): deterministic K1 weight gradient at measured slow or less accurate token counts on sm_100a / sm_103a (#8326)

## Summary

The Cake dense projection GEMM family covers BF16-input dense and
batched projection GEMMs (BF16 or FP32 weight-gradient output). It also
covers an FP32 router GEMM (256 experts, BF16x3 emulation). In
`flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_gemm`, a keyword-only
`deterministic` flag selects the variant. `deterministic=True` (the
default) calls `flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_det_gemm`.
`deterministic=False` runs the split-K / stream-K programs (#8190,
#8238).

This PR changes only the planner. It affects only `deterministic=False`
and only the projection weight gradient (K1). It applies to `sm_100a`
(GB200) and `sm_103a` (GB300) parts with 152 or more SMs.

Before this PR (#8190), these rows run a two-split program at every
token count. This PR runs the deterministic program instead at 76
measured (row, output type, token count) points. It also runs the
deterministic program at the token counts between two consecutive such
points of a row. On four `sm_103a` rows (BF16 output, `5120 -> 32, 48,
64, 128`), it also runs the deterministic program at every token count
above 65536. The measured token counts are 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192,
16231, 32768 and 65536.

The 76 points fall into two groups:

- **68 points:** the two-split program was not faster than the
deterministic program in every run. At these points, the deterministic
program keeps the backward pass and the checkpointed step within 1.3 %
of the two-split program.
- **8 points:** `sm_103a`, BF16 output, `5120 -> 32, 48, 64, 128` at
32768 and 65536 tokens. At these points, the two-split program's BF16
error (relative to its error budget) was up to 1.31x the deterministic
program's for some input seeds, on both GPUs. These 8 points become
slower than before (see below).

All other token counts, parts with fewer than 152 SMs, `sm_107a` and all
kernels are unchanged.

**Speedups**

Geomean over the 76 rows of each op, CUDA graph replay; range in
parentheses:

- wgrad: previous/new 1.051 (0.920 to 1.356); SOTA/new 0.748 (0.560 to
1.142).
- bwd: previous/new 1.030 (0.955 to 1.188); SOTA/new 0.740 (0.562 to
1.083).
- 2fwd+bwd: previous/new 1.009 (0.977 to 1.061); SOTA/new 0.579 (0.364
to 1.055).

det/new is 1.000 on every row, because the new plan runs the
deterministic program at these points (the new column is the det Cake
measurement; see Baselines). The eager previous/new geomeans are wgrad
1.052, bwd 1.030 and 2fwd+bwd 1.009. The largest gains are `sm_103a`
`5120 -> 128` and `6144 -> 128` at 512 tokens (graph wgrad previous/new
1.32 to 1.36, bwd 1.17 to 1.19).

The 8 accuracy points are slower than the previous version. Their graph
previous/new is 0.920 to 0.977 (wgrad), 0.955 to 0.986 (bwd) and 0.977
to 0.993 (2fwd+bwd). Among the other 68 points, the previous version is
faster in some rows. The lowest previous/new values are graph 0.977
(wgrad), 0.987 (bwd) and 0.994 (2fwd+bwd), and eager 0.969, 0.988 and
0.992.

In graph replays the library is faster than the new plan in 56 of the 76
rows for wgrad and bwd and in 67 for 2fwd+bwd, including every row below
8192 tokens. In eager mode, the library's bwd and 2fwd+bwd are
host-bound at small token counts (eager SOTA/new geomean 1.838 bwd,
1.631 2fwd+bwd). For this reason, the graph rows are the fair comparison
and come first in the table.

- **Rows:** 456 = 76 points x 3 ops x 2 modes. Graph rows (228) come
first, then eager rows (228). There is one row per point, op and mode.
- **Ops:** wgrad = weight gradient [d_out, d_in] from BF16 activations
[T, d_in] and BF16 output gradients [T, d_out], BF16 or FP32 output
(column "out"); bwd = input gradient (BF16 out) + wgrad; 2fwd+bwd =
checkpointed step (2 x forward + bwd). All Cake arms share the forward
and input-gradient programs. **Modes:** e = eager, g = CUDA graph
replay.
- **Latency:** median us over 2 to 6 runs per row. Each run is on one
GPU, with 9 paired groups (15 in a rerun); every row was measured on two
GPUs. GB300 used four GPUs in all: the reruns of `sm_103a` `4096 -> 32`
BF16, `5120 -> 32` FP32 and `6144 -> 32` FP32 at 512 tokens ran on two
other GPUs than their first runs. The time is the CUPTI GPU time of the
operation (first kernel begin to last kernel end, all launches). L2 is
cold before every iteration.
- **Baselines:** det Cake = `deterministic=True`. previous Cake =
`deterministic=False` before this PR (the #8190 plan). new =
`deterministic=False` with this PR; it runs the deterministic program at
every point in the table, so new us is the det Cake measurement (the
`deterministic=False` call that dispatches to that program was not timed
separately). SOTA = for wgrad, the fastest correct launch among
`torch.mm` and the cuBLASLt heuristic's top-8 algorithms; for bwd and
2fwd+bwd, the fastest correct library launch per op. Ratio = baseline us
/ new us; above 1.00 = this PR is faster.
- **Setup:** GB200, `sm_100a`, 152 SMs, driver 580.126.20; GB300,
`sm_103a`, 152 SMs, driver 580.159.03; CUDA 13.4 (nvcc 13.4.92), PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130, cuBLAS 13.8.0.4.
- **Noise:** per row, the interquartile range of the per-run
previous/new ratio has a median of 0.006, a 90th percentile of 0.016 and
a maximum of 0.10 (eager). Ratios within about 1 % of 1.00 are inside
this spread.

The family's other Cake variant is the deterministic package
`flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_det_gemm`
(`deterministic=True`) for the same projection and router GEMMs. Both
packages ship on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a; this PR changes the
`deterministic=False` plan on sm_100a and sm_103a only.

### [dcc8e67](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/dcc8e677c7a7e0ca6f6e61f12bc9259c264d3e88)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T16:22:03Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm_det): faster H 256 dw reduce and dc main, register-compensated H 1536 backward (#8319)

This PR changes the non-residual backward pass of the deterministic Cake
RMSNorm training package (`cake_rmsnorm_det_train`). The package covers
BF16 and FP32 weights, residual and non-residual inputs, row widths H
256 (per-head view) / 512 / 1536 / 2048 / 4096 / 5120 / 6144, and both
forward and backward passes. It adds new kernels for two large-row-count
routes. The first is H 256 backward (contiguous rows, key view
[T,4,256], query view [T,24,256], BF16 and FP32 weight) above 80896 rows
on sm_100a, 40960 rows on sm_103a and 70656 rows on sm_107a. That route
now splits the dw column reduction over more thread blocks, and on
sm_100a and sm_107a it also uses a lighter load pipeline in the main
backward kernel. The second is H 1536 backward with the compensated dw
sum, which now keeps its compensation terms in registers: FP32 weight
above 40448 rows on sm_103a, and BF16 and FP32 weight above 45056 rows
on sm_107a. Every row is faster than both the previous Cake package and
torch.compile (listed in that order):
- B200 (sm_100a), H 256: 1.046x-1.085x and 1.056x-1.181x.
- GB300 (sm_103a), H 256: 1.006x-1.052x and 1.029x-1.330x; H 1536 FP32
weight: 1.012x-1.019x and 1.407x-1.525x.
- R200 (sm_107a), H 256: 1.051x-1.153x and 1.132x-1.613x; H 1536 BF16
weight: 1.013x-1.023x and 1.483x-1.570x; H 1536 FP32 weight:
1.020x-1.024x and 4.067x-4.384x.

**NVIDIA B200 (148 SMs), sm_100a**; CUDA 13.4 (kernels built with nvcc
13.4), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0. Backward pass. Latency =
CUPTI kernel-active time per call, cold L2, median of 4 x 20 calls per
process. Previous Cake = the previously shipped Cake package; Cake =
this package; both through the package's public backward entry point in
the same processes (counterbalanced). Each Cake value = fastest measured
process over the row's formal sessions (4 sessions; each session a fresh
process set with fresh caches, one GPU per session). torch.compile =
fastest measured per-shape static compile (FP32 formula, dynamic=False;
minimum over every process of the formal sessions and a tc-only sweep,
each with a fresh inductor / Triton cache). Speedup = baseline / Cake.

### [a54d142](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/a54d14257df11b4ac0e114312905adbecbc94968)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T15:58:19Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mhc_det_train): per-SM capped ticket claim of the mapping pass at the uneven sm_100a rows (#8335)

This PR adds one schedule variant to the mHC training forward mapping
pass. This kernel is the first heavy kernel of `forward_prepare` (hidden
4096, bf16 input). The kernel already ships several schedule variants:

- Static programs: `nsx_st5_mb1`, `nsx`, `nsx_g2_ol2l`, `ns96_g2_ol2l`
- Tail-control forms: `nsx_ct`, `ns96_g2_ol2l_ct`
- Ticket form: `tk_nsx_g2_ol2l_ct`

The new variant is a ticket form with a per-SM cap:
`cake_mhc_det_train_fwd_map__tk_nsx_g2_ol2l_ct_ef_cap`. It is for
sm_100a only. It routes only at these uneven rows:

- 148 SMs: T 14209-16256 and 16513-18560
- 152 SMs: T 14593-16640 and 17025-19072

All other T keep the current program. Outputs are bitwise identical to
the static program. The deterministic training path uses this kernel.
The forward of the non-deterministic training path
(`cake_mhc_train_fwd_map__tk_nsx_g2_ol2l_ct_ef_cap`) routes the same
compiled kernel. Its sm_100a SASS is identical except for the symbol
name.

The variant fixes a slowdown of ~1.15-1.20x in `forward_prepare`. The
slowdown occurs at these token counts when a concurrent side stream
holds SMs (16 CTAs x 640 threads).

### [8e70727](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/8e70727da6ca0cad935108332001797585bdea9e)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T15:23:03Z
- **提交信息**: test(cake_mhc): with grad, nd tests follow the deterministic group-row forms (#8333)

Since #8256 and #8266 merged, 30 tests in
`tests/experimental/test_cake_mhc_train*.py` fail on main on sm_100a and
sm_103a. The nd package did not change. This PR changes only the tests.
It makes no package code changes.

**Background.** Cake's mHC training kernels have two packages. The
deterministic one is `flashinfer.cake_mhc_det_train_backend`. The opt-in
non-deterministic one, nd, is
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_mhc_train_backend` with
`deterministic=False`. nd is a standalone copy of the deterministic
registry, except for its backward finish. That finish is an atomic
column slab. Its dscale / dbase fold uses the deterministic per-CTA
reduction order, so nd's dscale / dbase were bitwise equal to the
deterministic ones.

Above 14927 tokens at hidden 4096 on sm_100a and sm_103a, #8256 runs the
deterministic backward's token owner and final reduction in group-row
forms (`BWD_ROW_BANDS`). dX and the other outputs keep their bits.
dscale and dbase sum the same terms in a different fixed order. #8266
adds an sm_100a column-slab program to the deterministic package. nd
does not copy the group-row forms because it has no reduction that reads
group-row partials.

The same 30 tests fail on GB200 (sm_100a) and GB300 (sm_103a):
- 11 GPU tests at hidden 4096, T >= 14928. They check dscale / dbase
bits against the deterministic backward and the workspace layout of the
parameter region.
- 19 registry-mirror tests. They cover the program set, record
vocabulary, routes, selection, PDL edges, workspace layout, host rules
and host plans.

**Changes** (`tests/experimental/test_cake_mhc_train.py`, `_graphs.py`,
`_rules.py`, `_workspace.py`):
- The registry mirrors leave out the deterministic group-row records,
`BWD_ROW_BANDS` / `bwd_group_rows`, and the host-plan keys `groups`,
`group_rows`, `param_dim0` and `param_dim1`. They also assert the
divergence explicitly. nd has no group-row record or rule. Inside the
band, the deterministic token owner is nd's per-CTA program plus
`_trows_dyn`. nd's `param_partial` is `[chunks, 32]` at every token
count.
- The selection, workspace and host-rule mirrors evaluate the
deterministic rules with `bwd_group_rows` off. Its caches are cleared on
entry and exit.
- On the GPU, dX must still be bitwise equal to the shipped
deterministic backward's. Inside the band, dscale / dbase are compared
bitwise with the deterministic backward run with its group-row forms
off. No tolerance is added.

**Results** (the six `tests/experimental/test_cake_mhc_train*.py`
files):
- On main before this PR: 30 failed / 693 passed / 3 skipped on GB200
(sm_100a) and 30 failed / 673 passed / 23 skipped on GB300 (sm_103a).
- With this PR on GB200: 0 failed / 723 passed / 3 skipped.
- With this PR and #8317 on current main (which includes #8304): 0
failed / 725 passed / 3 skipped on GB200 and 0 failed / 705 passed / 23
skipped on GB300.
- The skipped tests need two GPUs or a hidden size that has no two-size
column slab on sm_103a.

### [022f245](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/022f245cbea9a6dff1743c74b935f6a5576d2681)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T15:16:57Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_trtllm_mla_blackwell): cap FP8 page-64 reducer residency with a dynamic shared memory reservation (#8343)

`cake_trtllm_mla_blackwell` is the Cake MLA decode backend (TRT-LLM MLA
ABI) for DeepSeek-style MLA decode: 128 query heads, latent KV rank 512
+ RoPE 64 (QK dim 576, V dim 512), paged KV. It has 11 decode variants,
8 for BF16 KV and 3 for FP8 e4m3 KV with BF16 output. This PR changes
only the FP8 page-64 split-KV variant. Its reducer kernel used to launch
with 0 bytes of dynamic shared memory, so three reducer CTAs could be
resident per SM. This PR adds a 96 KiB dynamic shared memory reservation
that the reducer never uses, which limits each SM to two resident
reducer CTAs. Kernel code and arguments are unchanged. Compared with the
previous Cake version of the kernel, which FlashInfer main ships, it is
1.033x to 1.088x faster on the shapes below (FP8 e4m3 Q and KV, BF16
output, page size 64).

**NVIDIA B200 (Blackwell, sm_100a), CUDA 13.4**

| Shape | main latency (us) | this PR latency (us) | Speedup (main / PR)
|
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| batch 1, q_len 16, KV length 4096 | 17.153 | 16.352 | 1.049x |
| batch 2, q_len 16, KV length 4096 | 23.648 | 22.816 | 1.037x |
| batch 1, q_len 8, KV length 4096 | 16.224 | 14.912 | 1.088x |
| batch 1, q_len 16, KV length 2048 | 14.176 | 13.376 | 1.060x |

**NVIDIA GB300 (Blackwell, sm_103a), CUDA 13.4**

| Shape | main latency (us) | this PR latency (us) | Speedup (main / PR)
|
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| batch 1, q_len 16, KV length 4096 | 16.000 | 15.296 | 1.046x |
| batch 2, q_len 16, KV length 4096 | 22.560 | 21.856 | 1.033x |
| batch 1, q_len 8, KV length 4096 | 15.360 | 14.112 | 1.088x |
| batch 1, q_len 16, KV length 2048 | 13.216 | 12.544 | 1.054x |

The family's other Cake variants are the eight BF16 KV programs (CLC
persistent, CLC one-wave, two exact-shape CLC programs, native split-8
with PDL, value-half split, value-quarter split, tail) plus the FP8
page-32 variant with QK L2 hints and the FP8 tail; the whole family
ships on sm_100a (B200) and sm_103a (GB300).

### [e533411](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/e53341196bde63a60a145d0cb65044c02b2b00ba)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T15:09:19Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn_det): with grad, overlap the fused backward tail with multi-round split scans on B200 (#8342)

`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_det_train` is FlashInfer's
deterministic Gated DeltaNet chunked training kernel. It runs packed
variable-length training (forward + backward) on one GPU, and its
outputs and gradients are bitwise reproducible. The previous PR
overlapped the fused BF16-dbeta HV = 2H backward tail with the adjoint
scan on a side stream for single-round plans (sm_103a always; sm_100a
only when HV >= 32). This PR changes only the backward pass on sm_100a
(B200). There, the same overlap now also covers the second pass of a
split adjoint scan plan, at any HV. A split plan runs a pre-scan and a
stitch, then a second scan pass whose segments x HV CTAs outnumber the
SMs, so that pass runs in more than one round. The pre-scan and stitch
finish before the fork. The tail starts once the last CTA of the second
pass has started, so it never takes an SM that a scan CTA still needs.
The overlap is used only when the call carries at least 393216 (3 x
2^17) total tokens x value heads. Below that floor the call is
host-bound, so the overlap's extra host work would outlast its GPU
saving, and those calls keep the previous launches. Every other case
runs the same launches as before: serial plans, split plans with at most
as many CTAs as SMs, sm_103a, sm_107a, and calls under CUDA graph
capture. Outputs and gradients are bitwise identical to the previous
version. The baseline is the previous version of this kernel on current
FlashInfer main (speedup = main / this PR, so >1 is faster; median over
56 interleaved cells). On B200, forward + backward on the 7 x ~4.3k real
pack with H / HV 8 / 16 drops from 1.1118 to 1.0731 ms (1.036x). All
other B200 rows are unchanged within noise (0.993x to 1.002x on f+b).
GB300 is unchanged (1.000x f+b on every row), and the forward pass is
unchanged.

### [c258c2d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c258c2dd23ae7ffdab3f673e444b6dcfd6a763ec)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T15:06:05Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_deepgemm_mega_mhc): chain-packing programs for sm_107a FP8 launches on 208-SM devices (#8341)

`flashinfer.mega_mhc` (`prepare_mega_mhc`) runs the fused
manifold-constrained hyper-connection (mHC) inference step. FlashInfer
main ships 44 per-arch programs for it:

- 14 hidden-5120 FP8-E4M3-output programs on sm_100a and sm_103a.
- For hidden 4096, five programs on each of sm_107a, sm_100a and
sm_103a: BF16 output, its tailpipe twin, its weight-staging tailpipe
twin, FP8 group-128 output and NVFP4 output.
- Four sm_107a-only tailpipe and weight-staging tailpipe forms of the
FP8 group-128 and NVFP4 variants.
- Three sm_107a-only FP8 group-128 UE8M0-scale-mode programs (plain,
tailpipe and weight-staging tailpipe).
- One sm_107a-only fast-division form of the plain FP8 group-128
program.
- Six sm_107a-only fast-chain forms: one each of the BF16-output
tailpipe program, the plain FP8 group-128 program (raw scale mode), the
plain FP8 group-128 program (UE8M0 scale mode), the FP8 group-128
weight-staging tailpipe program (raw scale mode), the FP8 group-128
UE8M0 tailpipe program and the NVFP4 tailpipe program.
- One sm_107a-only chain-packing form of the FP8 group-128 tailpipe
program (raw scale mode).

This PR adds one sm_107a-only program. It also moves sm_107a
non-deterministic routes on 208-SM devices to the chain-packing
programs. The existing programs do not change.

- **Chain-packing form of the plain FP8 group-128 UE8M0 program (new).**
This form uses the same change as the existing chain-packing form of the
tailpipe program. The one-wave schedule packs the tokens of the fifth
round of the coefficient chain four per CTA. Outputs are bitwise
identical to the plain UE8M0 program.
- **SM-count key on routes.** A route can now carry an optional SM-count
key. Such a route serves only devices whose SM count is listed. With any
other SM count, or with none given, dispatch is exactly as on main. The
loader passes the device's SM count.
- **Raw scale mode, 208-SM devices, T = 929–968.** These launches move
from the FP8 group-128 tailpipe program to its chain-packing form.
- **UE8M0 scale mode, 208-SM devices, T = 930–936 and T = 952–968.**
These launches move from the plain FP8 group-128 UE8M0 program to its
new chain-packing form.

The change applies only to 208-SM devices. On the 208-SM device, the
fifth-round chain tokens start to overflow at T = 929. On the 216-SM
device, this starts at T = 969, where main already routes the raw scale
mode to the chain-packing form. On the 216-SM GPU, these token counts
keep their program, and dispatch does not change at all.

Every other launch keeps the program main dispatches. No sm_100a or
sm_103a launch changes. The deterministic mode does not change.

The moved launches are non-deterministic launches of the plain regime.
They keep their 13 splits and their launch. Outputs are bitwise
identical, and batch invariance does not change.

The baseline is the previous Cake version of the kernel, which is what
FlashInfer main dispatches today. A is the program main dispatches, and
B is the program this PR dispatches. Speedup = A / B. Both sides run
through FlashInfer's loader on the same GPU, with the same inputs, in
one process. Both use programmatic dependent launch, as main already
does. The tables show medians. Each table lists the owner shapes first,
then the changed rows. The 216-SM tables show only the owner shapes,
because no 216-SM launch changes.

- Chain-packing form of the FP8 group-128 tailpipe program, raw scales,
non-deterministic, T = 929–968 (13 splits): 1.031–1.104× on the 208-SM
GPU.
- Chain-packing form of the plain FP8 group-128 UE8M0 program, UE8M0
scales, non-deterministic (13 splits): 1.025–1.027× at T = 930–936 and
1.053–1.065× at T = 952–968 on the 208-SM GPU.
- Owner-shape rows, which keep their program: 0.994–1.003× on the 208-SM
GPU and 0.997–1.003× on the 216-SM GPU. None of the owner shapes is a
changed row.

NVIDIA R200 (sm_107a), 208 SMs, driver 615.71.10, CUDA 13.4 (nvcc
13.4.92), SM clock 2382–2411 MHz.**

### [2757266](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/2757266b2a42a54b217bd06092ff702e35f32f4f)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T15:03:23Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_lm_head_loss): skip the zero-gradient rows of the log-probability backward (#8268)

The Cake chunked LM-head + loss training backend has two forms. The
deterministic form, `flashinfer.experimental.cake_lm_head_det_loss`, is
the default. The non-deterministic form is
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_lm_head_loss`; you select it with
`deterministic=False` on the `flashinfer.chunked_lm_head` entries
(#8193). Both forms serve four entries: CE loss, policy loss, log-prob
and candidate-support. This PR changes only the backward of the
non-deterministic log-prob entry. The backward now skips rows whose
upstream gradient `dlogp` is zero, such as masked tokens. One device
kernel moves the rows with nonzero `dlogp` to the front and keeps their
count on the device. The GEMMs stop at that count. Nothing is read back
to the host, so the call stays CUDA-graph capturable. The skip applies
from 4097 rows per call on sm_100a and sm_103a. Smaller calls take the
unchanged path.

Headline results are for the cooled state and log-prob rows with T >=
8117 and some zero rows (16 rows per operation per GPU). ND = the
non-deterministic form with this PR. "Checkpointed" = 2x forward +
backward.

- **vs skip off (the #8193 path):**
- B200: backward 1.076x-1.943x, forward + backward 1.062x-1.574x,
checkpointed 1.042x-1.407x. All rows are ND faster except 1 inconclusive
checkpointed row.
- GB300: backward 1.120x-1.920x, forward + backward 1.090x-1.554x,
checkpointed 1.069x-1.394x. All rows are ND faster.
- **vs deterministic Cake:**
- B200: backward 1.072x-1.941x, forward + backward 1.054x-1.564x,
checkpointed 1.042x-1.405x. All rows are ND faster except 1 inconclusive
checkpointed row.
- GB300: backward 1.124x-1.926x, forward + backward 1.092x-1.557x,
checkpointed 1.072x-1.393x. All rows are ND faster.
- **vs CCE (results are mixed):**
- B200: backward 0.766x-1.292x (6 faster, 10 slower), forward + backward
0.876x-1.304x (6 faster, 9 slower, 1 parity), checkpointed 0.950x-1.284x
(7 faster, 4 slower, 4 inconclusive, 1 parity). The B200 wins over CCE
are at 50 % zero rows.
- GB300: backward 0.760x-1.282x (8 faster, 8 slower), forward + backward
0.895x-1.293x (8 faster, 8 slower), checkpointed 0.956x-1.261x (8
faster, 4 slower, 3 inconclusive, 1 parity).
- **No zero rows (T >= 8117):**
- vs skip off: B200 0.986x-1.007x (parity or inconclusive, none slower).
GB300 0.994x-1.000x (all parity).
- The call still runs the row ordering and the counted GEMMs. On B200
this costs up to about 1 % of backward time at large T, which is within
the noise band. For example, at T = 65031 one step went from 243.2 ms to
246.3 ms.
- CCE is faster than ND here: backward 0.693x-0.721x on B200 and
0.702x-0.714x on GB300.
- **Below the threshold, and controls:**
- T = 2048 (below 4097 rows) is at parity with skip off and with
deterministic Cake on both GPUs.
- The control rows (CE loss at T = 8117, policy loss at T = 32463) are
parity or inconclusive, none slower.

Method: H = 6144, V = 154880, BF16 X and W, Cake chunk 4096. About 5 %
of rows are ignored, and the valid counts are in the row labels. "Zero
rows" is the fraction of valid rows with `dlogp` = 0, placed in 512-row
groups or at random. Calls run eagerly, and L2 is flushed before every
call. Each call's latency is its CUPTI GPU span. The tables show the
cooled state, which adds a delay of 1.0x the back-to-back median before
each call. Latency is the median over steps of each step's median.
Speedup = baseline latency / ND latency, so > 1 means ND is faster.
Brackets are hierarchical-bootstrap CI95. A row is "ND faster" or "ND
slower" only when the CI95 lies outside 1 ± max(1 %, A/A floor) and
every per-step ratio is on the same side of 1. A row is "parity" when
the whole CI95 is inside that band, and "inconclusive" otherwise.
Steps/nodes per row are in the last column. The deterministic Cake
baseline is `cake_lm_head_det_loss` at the same FlashInfer head. The
non-Cake baseline is Cut Cross-Entropy (CCE) 25.1.1 with
`torch_compile`, unchunked, so it keeps the full T x V logits. #8193
established CCE as the strongest non-Cake peer for the log-prob entry.
"Skip off" is the same head with the skip turned off, i.e. the #8193
path. The CE-loss and policy-loss rows are controls for entries this PR
does not change. They have no non-Cake column here; their non-Cake
comparisons are in #8193. Software: CUDA 13.4 toolkit, PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130.

The d1 state adds a 2 ms delay before each call. It was run on the same
rows but is not tabulated. In d1, no row is slower than skip off or
deterministic Cake on either GPU. At T >= 8117 with zero rows, compared
with skip off:

- B200: backward 16/16 faster (1.079x-1.897x), forward + backward 14
faster and 2 inconclusive (1.050x-1.548x), checkpointed 14 faster and 2
inconclusive (1.059x-1.397x).
- GB300: all 48 rows faster (backward 1.108x-1.880x, forward + backward
1.093x-1.560x, checkpointed 1.067x-1.392x).

The deterministic form and the other non-deterministic entries are
unchanged, both forms ship for sm_100a (B200 / GB200) and sm_103a (B300
/ GB300), and sm_107a (R200) support for the non-deterministic form is
in #8282, which does not include this skip yet.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Performance**
* Added an optional backward optimization that skips work for rows with
exactly zero upstream gradient. It defaults to calls with at least 4,097
rows and can be disabled; unsupported plans continue using the existing
behavior.
* **Documentation**
* Documented when the optimization applies, how rows are handled, and
how non-finite values affect it.
* **Tests**
* Added coverage for row ordering, chunk counts, threshold behavior,
repeated calls, CUDA graph replay, and edge cases.

### [33ddcba](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/33ddcbacf7b7b27bf3d068de20745d21cf268f50)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T15:02:29Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsa_indexer_det): use unpaired l6 scan for sampling-off calls <= 16384 queries (#8339)

`flashinfer.dsa_indexer.dsa_indexer_det_topk` is the Cake deterministic
DSA indexer top-k scan. It ships in the package
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_dsa_indexer_det`. It uses BF16 queries and
keys, and FP32 head weights and scores. It returns the top-k key ids for
each query. The ids and scores do not depend on partition or chunking.
Ties go to the larger id. Cake ships one variant of this kernel. This PR
changes which scan program the host picks for some sampling-off calls on
sm_100a and sm_103a.

This PR changes host-side program choice only. Kernel sources and the
compiled package do not change.

- It adds the policy field `l6_solo_unsampled_max_queries`. It is 16384
on sm_100a and sm_103a. It is unset on sm_107a.
- In sampling-off mode, the sampled first threshold is off. Some
sampling-off calls have a plan that runs the CTA-pair l6 scan program
unsplit. If such a call has at most 16384 queries, it now runs the
unpaired l6 scan program instead.
- Sampled calls do not change. The wide, narrow and split plans do not
change. sm_107a does not change.
- The limit is 16384 queries because on GB200, longer full-causal calls
with sink statistics and 2 or more segments ran 1.4 to 2.3 % slower with
the unpaired program, while at most 16384 queries every measured shape
was faster or unchanged within noise on GB200 and GB300.

The baseline is the previous Cake version of this package on FlashInfer
main. Speedup is main time divided by this PR time. We measured each
shape in sampled mode and in sampling-off mode. Each GPU has 64 ratios,
from 32 shapes in two modes. Output bits match main on every shape.

| GPU | min | median | max |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GB300 (sm_103a) | 0.995x | 1.002x | 1.095x |
| GB200 (sm_100a) | 0.988x | 1.001x | 1.071x |

In sampling-off mode, some rows now run the unpaired l6 program instead
of the CTA-pair l6 program. On GB300, their sampling-off speedups are:

P2 1.029x, P1 1.022x and P1sink 0.998x. All other rows run the same
program as main. Their times do not change beyond noise.

### [f8ef891](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/f8ef891e8676d26b37bbf07eb9e985e5c258b6f9)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T15:01:46Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kimi_k3_latent_moe): faster Kimi-K3 LatentMoE TP8 and TP1 multi-partial decode tails on GB200 and GB300 (#8340)

This PR updates the Cake programs for the Kimi-K3 Stable LatentMoE front
and tail projections of one rank in
`flashinfer.experimental.kimi_k3_latent_moe` (BF16, `sm_100a` and
`sm_103a`). The package has four variants: the front and the tail
projection, each for TP1 and TP8. Decode-sized token counts run a decode
instance, and the tail fuses the RMSNorm and the reduction of P routed
partials into it. Larger token counts run a prefill GEMM. The baseline
is the Cake programs on FlashInfer main as of #8263 ("previous").
Speedup = previous / this PR. This PR changes routes of the TP8 and TP1
decode tail variants on NVIDIA GB300 (`sm_103a`) and NVIDIA GB200
(`sm_100a`). Two sets of rows now run a new global-y split-row tail
instance: TP8 rows of 5 to 32 tokens with 2 or more routed partials, and
TP1 rows of 9 to 32 tokens with 8 or more routed partials. In this
instance, the four epilogue warps share each row's partial sum, rounding
and stores, and the routed partials are prefetched into L2. Its outputs
stay bitwise those of the previous program. On the TP8 rows timed alone
the speedup is 1.05x to 1.37x on GB300 and 1.04x to 1.38x on GB200. On
the TP1 rows timed alone it is 1.03x to 1.05x on GB300 and 1.02x to
1.05x on GB200. The routes on B200 and B300 do not change.

Rows with "—" under "Preceding work" time the tail row alone. The same
runs also measured some rows right after a preceding kernel: "none"
means with no predecessor work, and "front" means after the front
projection.

### [cac5cec](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/cac5cec500a3e1071fe44585eeab9dbc810dbe49)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T14:57:29Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn): run ragged SM107 FP32-state prefill batches bounded by their longest sequence on the DV-split body (up to 1.17x) (#8338)

`chunk_gated_delta_rule(backend="cake_gdn")` runs the Cake GDN prefill.
The kernel ships 254 prefill records: 115 on sm_100a, 107 on sm_103a and
111 on sm_107a (one record can serve several architectures). With BF16
I/O, the state is FP32 (88 records), BF16 (59), FP16 (6), FP8 E4M3 (6)
or FP8 E5M2 (6). With FP16 I/O, the state is FP32 (89). Each record is a
full-DV body or a DV-split body.

This PR changes route selection on sm_107a only. It applies to ragged
prefill batches with BF16 I/O, FP32 initial and final state, host
lengths (`cu_seqlens_cpu`), no checkpoints or state indices, and a size
over the DV-split tile budget (2 * num_seqs * max(Hq, Hv) > 212). On
main, such a batch runs the full-DV record of its key. With this PR, the
batch runs the DV-split record of the same key, with one CTA per half
tile, when this O(1) host-integer rule holds: `max(Hq, Hv) *
(total_seq_len + 384 * num_seqs) <= max_seq_len * (90 if the first
sequence is the longest else 20)`. The rule applies to 15 sm_107a
full-DV records (Hq/Hv 2/4, 2/8, 4/8, 4/16, 8/16, 8/32, 16/32, 16/64).
Every other call resolves and launches as on main.

The baseline is the previous Cake route on FlashInfer main at
`c07e9181007063b152eaef946bdf1acbc05d481a`, which is the full-DV record
of the same key. The route changes on 9 of the 70 owner shapes. On these
9 shapes, the GPU span ratio is 1.1043-1.1699x, and one eager call takes
10.27-28.03 µs less (paired median).

*NVIDIA VR200 (Rubin), sm_107a, 212 SMs, driver 620.43; CUDA 13.4, torch
2.14.1+cu130. BF16 I/O, FP32 initial and final state, `cu_seqlens_cpu`
passed. main = FlashInfer main at `c07e918`; new = this PR. GPU span is
the CUPTI kernel span of one call with a cold L2; each of two runs
(seeds 17 and 29) takes the median of interleaved, counterbalanced
main/new samples, the column gives the mean of the two medians, and
main/new gives the range of the per-run ratios (above 1 means this PR is
faster). Whole call is the CUDA-event time of one eager call with the
GPU idle before the call; main, an A/A control and new are loaded in one
process and rotated per call with fresh lengths, each value is the
median of all 1800 calls over 6 rounds, and new-main and A/A are medians
[p10, p90] of per-call paired differences. "fail closed, both" rows
raise on both sides in the timed configuration; their whole-call times
use the default route.*

Calls that keep their route launch the same kernels (GPU span main/new
0.9978-1.0028 on the 47 such rows with a GPU span), but they use a
little more host time: per row, the paired new-main median of one eager
call is -0.03 to 0.42 µs, while the A/A median band is [-0.51, 0.06] µs.

The other variants (FP16 I/O; BF16, FP16 and FP8 state; and every call
on sm_100a and sm_103a) resolve and launch as on main, and the family
ships on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

Co-authored-by: Yingyi Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [40f9252](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/40f92526b5c6a513720ddb97f04a491462561d73)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T14:53:37Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mok_bf16): re-render the sm_107a MXFP8 autograd kernels (#7821) (#8302)

This PR re-renders the eight sm_107a (Rubin) MXFP8 libraries of
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_mok_bf16`, for #7821. This package is the
MoK fused persistent MegaMoE training kernel exposed through
`flashinfer.mok`. The eight libraries are forward, recompute, backward,
and backward with FP32 weight gradients, each in a plain and a clamped
version. The MXFP8 block-scale ring now keeps its own cursor. This keeps
the combine output bitwise deterministic when BF16 shared-expert tiles
interleave with routed MXFP8 tiles under tile stealing. Macro batches
after the first now pipeline the forward dispatch. The kept sm_107a
entries move to the CUDA 13.4 floor that Rubin needs. A new test checks
that MXFP8 forward reruns are bitwise identical.

**MXFP8: previous version vs this PR**, previous / new (speedup)

replay (ms) | Backward (ms) | Microbatch (ms) | Training update (ms) |

*NVIDIA Vera Rubin (VR NVL72, sm_107a, 212 SMs), 8 GPUs (2 trays x 4,
one NVLink domain), driver 620.69, CUDA 13.4, PyTorch 2.14.1. Shape:
hidden 4096, intermediate 2048, 288 experts, top-8, one shared expert,
clamped SwiGLU limit 10, EP8, FP32 weight gradients, default `auto`
communication split. Previous = this package on FlashInfer main (commit
9643349fca). Times in ms: per-round medians (6 rounds), max over ranks,
averaged over two runs of each version measured in A-B-B-A order on the
same nodes with the same inputs. Microbatch = MXFP8 weight quantization
+ scheduling + forward + full-forward checkpoint replay + backward.
Training update = MoE part of one optimizer update: 5 layers x 2
microbatches. Peak memory = per-rank peak above resident memory for one
microbatch, max over ranks. Speedup = previous / new; values below 1.00x
are slower.*

This PR does not re-render the BF16 variants or the sm_100a and sm_103a
libraries. The package still ships forward, recompute and backward
programs for all 8 training variants (BF16 or MXFP8, SwiGLU or clamped
SwiGLU, BF16 or FP32 weight-gradient accumulator) on sm_100a, sm_103a
and sm_107a, which is 48 libraries per architecture.
