### [2704749](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/2704749a8fe1fe10c4cf4018c5678cb7e17f30fc)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T14:49:17Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mhc): GB200 PDL bands for the non-deterministic mHC autograd kernels (#8317)

This PR adds GB200-specific launch bands for three edges of Cake's mHC
(manifold-constrained hyper-connections) training kernel. Cake's mHC
training kernel has a deterministic mode and an opt-in non-deterministic
mode, nd (`deterministic=False` of
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_mhc_train`). Some nd kernel launches
use programmatic dependent launch (PDL), which lets the dependent kernel
launch before its predecessor finishes. Per call, PDL is turned on or
off by token-count (T) bands, set per architecture, edge (predecessor ->
dependent kernel) and call path. #8281 added the nd package's own bands,
keyed by (architecture, SM count, hidden size), with B200 (148 SMs)
entries. #8304 added GB300 entries. Neither applies to GB200.

The new GB200 (sm_100a, 152 SMs) entries cover three edges. Before this
PR, GB200 used the deterministic package's bands (the sm_100a defaults)
on all three, with PDL on elsewhere:
- forward collapse (K1 -> K3, forward path): PDL off for T = 4097..8192;
- checkpointed backward prepare (K1 -> K5, checkpoint path): PDL off for
T = 4097..8192;
- checkpointed column slab (K6 -> K7, checkpoint path): PDL off for T =
1025..8192.

With this PR:
- **Forward collapse and checkpointed backward prepare on GB200:** at
every hidden size, PDL is now off for T = 2945..3584 and 4097..8192. The
2945..3584 band is new. On 152 SMs, those token counts are 24 to 28
token tiles of 128.
- **Column slab on GB200:** PDL is now off for
- hidden 4096: T = 1025..2159, so it is on from T = 2160 (before, it was
off up to 8192);
  - hidden 5120: T = 1025..1984 and 7169..8192;
  - hidden 7168: from T = 769 up.
- **Unchanged launches:** the backward from saved statistics and the
other GB200 edges. B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs), GB300 and B300 (sm_103a) and
sm_107a launch exactly as before.
- **Unchanged outputs:** PDL is a scheduling attribute, and the same
programs run on the same buffers.

**Speedup vs the previous nd version.** "new" is nd with this PR.
"previous" is the same build with the nd package's own bands removed. On
GB200 that is exactly how nd launched before this PR, including with
#8281 and #8304. The table lists only the 111 rows where the two launch
differently: forward at T = 2945..3584 (9 per hidden size) and
checkpointed step (24 at hidden 4096, 28 at 5120, 32 at 7168). The
backward from saved statistics, and the forward outside T = 2945..3584,
launch identically, so they are not listed.

How the first table was timed:
- All arms run in one process on the same inputs, in ABBA (mirrored)
order inside each group.
- Each arm replays a CUDA graph of the operation after a 512 MiB L2
flush. Forward rows replay the forward, and checkpointed-step rows
replay the checkpointed step.
- Latency is the median over 16 groups of the per-group mean of 30
replays.
- "previous" is timed in two arms. The table shows the first arm, and
the gap between the two arms is the null.
- Speedup = previous / new. Above 1 means new is faster.
- Compare ratios within a table. This timing differs from the
two-baseline tables.

This branch was merged with FlashInfer main, without a rebase. The first
table's hidden 4096 and 5120 rows were measured on the code of this PR's
head (its second commit). Its hidden 7168 rows were measured on the
first commit. The second commit changes only the hidden 4096 and 5120
column-slab bands, so the hidden 7168 rows run the same launches as the
second commit. The merge with main does not change the launches this
table compares. The two-baseline tables were measured on the merged
head.

100 rows are faster, 10 are at parity and 1 is slower:
- forward, T = 2945..3584: all rows are faster. Hidden 4096 reads 1.031
to 1.042 (2.83 to 3.89 us faster), hidden 5120 1.030 to 1.040 (3.22 to
4.79 us faster) and hidden 7168 1.036 to 1.040 (5.07 to 6.39 us faster).
- checkpointed step, hidden 4096 (T = 2160..8192): 20 faster, 3 at
parity and 1 slower. The rows read 0.999 to 1.059 (up to 16.40 us
faster).
- checkpointed step, hidden 5120 (T = 1985..7168): 26 faster and 2 at
parity. The rows read 1.000 to 1.059 (up to 19.44 us faster).
- checkpointed step, hidden 7168 (T = 769..65536): 27 faster and 5 at
parity. The rows read 1.000 to 1.060 (up to 26.59 us faster).

The parity rows, all checkpointed step, as (speedup, groups in which new
is faster, null):
- hidden 4096 T = 3648: 1.000, 6 of 16, null 0.002 us;
- hidden 4096 T = 4097: 1.000, 11 of 16, null 0.10 us;
- hidden 4096 T = 8192: 1.000, 8 of 16, null 0.05 us;

The slower row is the hidden 4096 T = 4096 checkpointed step: 0.999 (new

NVIDIA GB200, sm_100a (152 SMs). Cake kernels: CUDA 13.4 toolkit, driver
580.126.20. X BF16 [T, 4, H], FP32 mapping, 4 streams, non-KCP.
CUDA-graph replay after a 512 MiB L2 flush, median of 16 ABBA groups x
30 replays. "previous" is the first of two arms.

**Baselines and method** for the two-baseline tables (one per hidden
size, T = 256 to 65536). They have 30 token counts at hidden 4096 and
5120 and 33 at 7168.
- **det:** the deterministic mode (`deterministic=True`) from the same
build: FlashInfer main merged into this PR, including #8256 and #8266.
It is the original deterministic Cake implementation, and this PR does
not change it.
- **det2:** a second det call timed in the same groups. A row is within
its own noise when it is below 1.000 vs det by at most its own |det2/det
- 1| (unrounded).
- **B0 (non-Cake SOTA):** per row, the faster of IEEE-FP32 eager PyTorch
and `torch.compile(fullgraph=False, dynamic=False)` of the same mHC
training function, with TF32 off. `torch.compile` won on every row, and
the parenthesis in the B0 column names the winner.
- **Why B0:** B0 is the strongest applicable baseline because it is the
only non-Cake implementation of this function at these sizes.
TransformerEngine's mHC (TF32 mapping math, log-domain Sinkhorn without
eps) and Megatron-LM's fused mHC (TF32 projection) compute a different
function. FlashInfer's `flashinfer.mhc` kernels and DeepGEMM's mega_mhc
are inference only.
- **Operations:** forward = forward prepare + forward finish. Backward =
backward prepare + backward finish from saved statistics. Checkpointed
step = forward + statistics recompute (`cake_mhc_train_forward_stats`) +
backward on the checkpoint path. For B0, the checkpointed step is a
no-grad forward + a with-grad forward + the backward.
- **Workload:** X BF16 [T, 4, H], FP32 mapping, 4 streams, non-KCP,
random inputs.
- **Speedup:** det or B0 latency / new latency. Above 1 means new is
faster.
- **Comparability:** on every row, the new forward outputs, dX and the
other backward outputs except dfn, dscale and dbase are bitwise equal to
det. dscale and dbase are bitwise equal to det at hidden 5120 and 7168,
and at hidden 4096 for T up to 8192. At hidden 4096 from T = 14928 (10
token counts), det now sums their terms in another fixed order, #8256's
group-row order. nd does not copy that order, so their last bits can
differ there. The new dfn relative L2 vs det is at most 8.73e-08 /
8.76e-08 / 8.68e-08 at hidden 4096 / 5120 / 7168. B0's dfn relative L2
vs det is at most 4.74e-06 / 4.83e-06 / 5.00e-06.

**Speedup vs det and B0.** Geomean speedups over each table's token
counts (forward / backward / checkpointed step):

| hidden | vs det | vs B0 |
|---|---|---|
| 4096 | 1.000 / 1.043 / 1.024 | 11.22 / 8.83 / 12.56 |
| 5120 | 1.001 / 1.047 / 1.030 | 12.84 / 8.69 / 13.59 |
| 7168 | 1.003 / 1.021 / 1.015 | 13.57 / 8.59 / 14.06 |

No row is slower than B0. The smallest speedup vs B0 is 6.82 (hidden
4096 forward, T = 256).

nd and det run the same forward programs, so forward rows near 1.000 vs
det are noise. The forward det null spread (max |det2/det - 1|) is 0.22
% / 1.55 % / 0.19 % at hidden 4096 / 5120 / 7168. In these eager tables,
the forward rows at T = 2945..3584 read about 1.000. The forward gain in
the first table is a CUDA-graph effect that eager launches do not show.

Eight backward and checkpointed-step rows are below 1.000 vs det. As
(speedup vs det, det2/det), they are:
- hidden 4096 backward T = 65536 (0.995, 0.999);
- hidden 5120 checkpointed step T = 65536 (0.997, 1.002);
- hidden 7168 backward T = 2976 (0.993, 1.000), 3456 (0.996, 1.002) and
49152 (0.998, 1.000);
- hidden 7168 checkpointed step T = 2976 (0.998, 1.000), 3200 (0.996,
0.999) and 3456 (0.996, 1.002).

None is within its own noise. For the hidden 7168 rows at T =
2976..3456, a separate eager run of the same build with 16 groups (same
statistic) read new faster than det. That run read backward 1.022 /
1.021 / 1.019 and checkpointed step 1.070 / 1.070 / 1.070 at T = 2976 /
3200 / 3456. In that run, det itself took 422.5 us for the checkpointed
step at T = 2976, vs 406.8 us in the table, so these rows vary between
processes. At T = 49152 the same run read backward 1.003 and
checkpointed step 1.000. At T = 65536 it read backward 1.010 and
checkpointed step 1.002.

### [1b1cf94](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/1b1cf945a9ae4ed6ffa48cf1f0b09f9a65db5d72)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T14:45:08Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_fmha): aligned hd256 q1 grouped paged decode programs for sm_100a / sm_103a (#8337)

Cake FMHA (`flashinfer.cake_fmha`) paged decode ships 19 decode
components. This PR adds one of them, `decode_aligned_bf16_hd256`. It
provides BF16 programs for single-query (q_len 1) grouped paged decode
at head dim 256, with eight query heads per KV head, page size 16 and
HND layout, on sm_100a and sm_103a. There are three programs: a
persistent program that runs one CTA per (request, KV head), and two
cluster programs that split each (request, KV head) over a cluster of 2
or 4 CTAs. The decode selector sends it only the rows marked "aligned
(new)" or "aligned cluster, 4 CTAs (new)", and that set differs between
B200 and GB300. Every other row keeps `decode_balanced_bf16_hd256`, the
previous Cake route and the baseline here. On the rows it takes, the new

### [0578b8d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/0578b8dbe5b33670d4e132e874fe5376744ecc23)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T14:42:51Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_gemm): leaner deterministic=False convenience path for the router GEMM (#8309)

The `flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_gemm` family has
BF16-input dense and batched projection GEMMs and an FP32 router GEMM
(256 experts, BF16x3 emulation). `deterministic=True` (the default)
calls `dense_projection_det_gemm`. `deterministic=False` runs the
split-K / stream-K programs of #8190, #8238, #8261 and #8275.

This PR cuts the host (CPU) cost of eager `deterministic=False` calls.
Programs, plans, split counts and numeric results do not change. Router
shapes without a measured plan now call the deterministic entry point
directly. Planned router launches bind arguments once per cache key.
They also convert the BF16x3 workspace once per growth. Each call reads
tensor metadata once. Few-token eager sequences are host bound, so the
GPU now waits less between launches.

Against previous Cake, router bwd is 1.060-1.395 (GB300) and 1.004-1.372
(GB200), largest at 5120 x 256, T 64. Router 2fwd+bwd is 1.050-1.177 and
1.020-1.185. Projection bwd is 1.035-1.078 and 2fwd+bwd 1.042-1.072. The
fwd rows (router and projection) are 1.000-1.009 (parity). CUDA graph
replays of prepared launches do not change: 0.995-1.011 (GB300) and
0.994-1.014 (GB200), over 28 cells per GPU.

Against det Cake, router 2fwd+bwd is still slower (0.898-0.933,
0.905-0.946). Router bwd is slower except 5120 x 256 at T 64 (1.026,
1.042). Router fwd is also slightly slower on every router row but one:
0.986-0.990 on all 5 GB300 rows and 0.995-0.999 on the 4 GB200 hidden
5120 rows; GB200 4096 x 256, T 64 is 1.010. Projection 4096 -> 128 is
slower (bwd 0.898 / 0.940, 2fwd+bwd 0.940 / 0.964). Projection 4096 ->
32 is faster (bwd 1.205 / 1.180, 2fwd+bwd 1.094 / 1.098).

Against SOTA, the library is faster on every projection row
(0.252-0.653) and every router bwd row (0.760-0.933). It is also faster
on router 2fwd+bwd at T 128-224 (0.756-0.818). At T 64, this PR is
faster (1.252-1.736), because the BF16x9 router forward takes
131.8-161.9 us. We did not measure plain FP32 `cublasSgemm`, which also
meets the router's accuracy budget. Thus router SOTA/new values above 1
can overstate the gap. R200 (`sm_107a`) runs the same host code but was
not measured.

- **Row:** one GPU, shape and op, measured as an eager call sequence of
the entry points (no prepared launch, no CUDA graph). There are 21 rows
per GPU and 42 in all.
- **Shapes:** router = FP32 router GEMM, hidden 4096 or 5120, 256
experts, T 64 to 224 tokens. Proj = BF16 dense projection 4096 -> 128 or
4096 -> 32, FP32 weight gradient, T 1024.
- **Ops:** fwd = forward GEMM. bwd = input gradient + weight gradient.
2fwd+bwd = checkpointed step (2 x fwd + bwd).
- **Latency:** median us of the CUPTI GPU interval of the op, from first
kernel begin to last kernel end. L2 is cold before every iteration.
- **Runs:** each run has 15 paired groups x 20 timed steps per arm, in
rotated arm order. A cell is the median of the per-run medians. GB300
has 8 runs on 2 nodes, one per GPU. GB200 has 4 runs on 1 node. On each
node, two runs use one long-lived process, and two runs use a new
process per row.
- **Baselines:** det Cake = `deterministic=True`. Previous Cake =
`deterministic=False` at 8f2f2f5e (#8261 and #8275 change only `sm_107a`
rows). SOTA (every GEMM of the op): router = cuBLAS 13.1.1 `cublasSgemm`
with `CUBLAS_FP32_EMULATED_BF16X9_MATH`; projection = `torch.mm` (cuBLAS
heuristic), FP32 weight-gradient output.
- **Ratio:** baseline us / new us. A value above 1.00 means this PR is
faster.
- **Setup:** NVIDIA GB300, `sm_103a`, 152 SMs, driver 580.159.03; NVIDIA
GB200, `sm_100a`, 152 SMs, driver 580.126.20; CUDA 13.4 (driver API);
PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130.

### [c34707a](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c34707ae98b8f2ff53a5ea2e98ac9b2cbc24b702)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T14:19:10Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate): non-deterministic mid- and long-input forwards on SM107 (#8332)

`cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate` computes `y = RMSNorm(x, w) * SiLU(z)` on BF16
rows of head dim 128 for training. It ships as two packages: a
deterministic package (`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_det_train`,
`deterministic=True`) and a non-deterministic package
(`deterministic=False`). The non-deterministic package uses rows per SM
(T × H / SM count) to choose one of its forwards: `fwd`, `fwd_short`,
`fwd_mid` or `fwd_long`. Its backwards write dw in BF16 or FP32, and
each comes in a short and a long form.

This PR changes only the non-deterministic forward on sm_107a. Until
now, that forward ran the deterministic forward program at every row
count. With this PR it runs `fwd_mid` from 800 rows per SM and
`fwd_long` from 1740 rows per SM. Below 800 rows per SM it still runs
the deterministic program. sm_100a and sm_103a do not change: they still
switch to `fwd_mid` at 976 rows per SM and to `fwd_long` at 2400. No
backward changes.

### Speedup

On R200 with 216 SMs, this PR was A/B-tested against the previous Cake
version on the same GPU, with 6 process pairs per row:

- `fwd` on the `fwd_long` shapes (7830x48 to 33000x48, 16384x32 and
32737x32): faster in all 6 pairs on every shape. new - previous ranges
from -1.904 to -11.880 µs; for example, 32737x48 takes 123.520 µs, down
from 135.393 µs. Against deterministic Cake: 1.058-1.095x.
- `fwd` on the `fwd_mid` shapes (3600x48 to 7700x48): faster in all 6
pairs at 3600x48, 4097x48, 4500x48 and 7700x48 (-0.064 to -0.448 µs).
Slower in all 6 pairs at 6000x48 (+0.032 µs). Against deterministic
Cake: 0.999-1.025x.
- `ckpt (CUDA graph)` on every shape from 800 rows per SM: faster in all
6 pairs, by -0.728 to -24.584 µs. Against deterministic Cake:
1.058-1.093x on the `fwd_mid` shapes and 1.048-1.086x on the `fwd_long`
shapes.
- Shapes below 800 rows per SM and every `bwd (CUDA graph)` row run the
same code as before. All of them read `overlap` in the A/B.

On R200 with 212 SMs, results come from a same-process run with no
previous-Cake arm:

- `fwd` on the `fwd_mid` shapes: 1.019-1.068x vs deterministic Cake and
0.958-0.985x vs the best non-Cake implementation.
- `fwd` on the `fwd_long` shapes: 1.105-1.169x vs deterministic Cake and
1.023-1.064x vs the best non-Cake implementation.
- `ckpt (CUDA graph)` on the `fwd_mid` shapes: 1.061-1.107x vs
deterministic Cake and 0.995-1.023x vs the best non-Cake implementation.
- `ckpt (CUDA graph)` on the `fwd_long` shapes: 1.067-1.100x vs
deterministic Cake and 1.001-1.035x vs the best non-Cake implementation.

On both board classes, `bwd` and `bwd (CUDA graph)` run the unchanged
non-deterministic backward. Their ratios therefore do not come from this
PR. `ckpt` includes that backward.

Rows below 1x or at parity:

- vs previous Cake (216 SMs): 6000x48 `fwd` takes 28.416 µs against
28.384 µs (+0.032 µs) and was slower in all 6 pairs. On the same shape,
`ckpt (CUDA graph)` was faster in all 6 pairs (-0.932 µs).
- vs deterministic Cake, 212 SMs: 1 of 104 rows is below 1x, 1x48 `ckpt
(CUDA graph)` at 0.998x (n.s.). `fwd` is at parity (1.000x (n.s.)) at
1x48, 7x48, 129x48, 2048x48 and 5088x32.
- vs deterministic Cake, 216 SMs: 4 of 66 rows are below 1x. These are
1x48 `ckpt (CUDA graph)` at 0.979x, plus `fwd` at 1031x48 (0.991x),
6000x48 (0.999x) and 5088x32 (0.996x). `fwd` is at parity (1.000x) at
1x48, 129x48 and 2048x48.
- vs the best non-Cake implementation (212 SMs only; non-Cake was not
measured with 216 SMs):
- `fwd` is below 1x on every shape that runs `fwd` or `fwd_mid`:
0.756-0.982x at H=48 and 0.946-0.985x at H=32.
- `ckpt (CUDA graph)` is below 1x at 1x48 (0.712x), 7x48 (0.884x),
3600x48 (0.999x), 4500x48 (0.997x), 6000x48 (0.995x) and 8192x32
(0.998x).
- `bwd` is below 1x at 33000x48 (0.990x, FLA) and at parity (1.000x) at
10600x48, 16384x48, 30193x48 and 16384x32.

### R200, 212 SMs

**NVIDIA R200 (sm_107a, 212 SMs), CUDA 13.4, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA
13.0), Triton 3.8.0.**

- Timing: CUPTI, cold L2, median of 10 per-round medians. Inputs are
BF16 [T, H, 128], eps 1e-6, BF16 dw.
- det Cake (the deterministic package) and new (the non-deterministic
package with this PR) are timed in the same process.
- Best non-Cake is the fastest per row of FLA 0.6.0 `rms_norm_gated`,
mamba_ssm v2.3.2 `rmsnorm_fn` and `torch.compile`. `torch.compile` runs
either in default mode or with mode `max-autotune-no-cudagraphs`, which
the table labels `torch.compile max-autotune`; both use `dynamic=False`.
- `ckpt` is the checkpointed step, 2 × fwd + bwd. `(CUDA graph)` rows
replay a CUDA graph. The non-Cake backwards were not captured in a CUDA
graph, so `bwd (CUDA graph)` has no non-Cake value (n/a).
- `vs det` = det / new and `vs non-Cake` = non-Cake / new. Above 1x
means new is faster. (n.s.) means not significant.
- There is no previous-Cake arm for this board class. Its rows are not
pooled with the 216-SM table.

### R200, 216 SMs

**NVIDIA R200 (sm_107a, 216 SMs), CUDA 13.4, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA
13.0).**

- A/B setup: 12 processes on one GPU (6 previous, 6 new), 10 rounds
each. Every process also times the deterministic package in the same
process.
- Each process value is the median of 10 round medians. Each cell is the
median [min..max] over processes: all 12 for det Cake, the 6 new
processes for new and the 6 previous processes for previous.
- Previous Cake is the non-deterministic package with the sm_107a
programs and host plan of FlashInfer `main` before this PR (after
#8301), which ran the deterministic forward program at every row count.
New is the non-deterministic package with this PR's sm_107a programs and
host plan.
- `fwd` is the CUPTI kernel span of the eager forward, with cold L2.
`(CUDA graph)` rows are the GPU span of a CUDA-graph replay. `ckpt` is 2
× fwd + bwd.
- `vs det` = det / new. Above 1x means new is faster.
- `new - previous` is the median [min..max] over the 6 pairs. A negative
value means new is faster. `pairs` counts pairs with new < previous /
new > previous.
- A/B: `FASTER` or `SLOWER` means every pair has the same sign and the
process values do not overlap. All other rows read `overlap`.
- Non-Cake implementations were not measured on this board class. Its
rows are not pooled with the 212-SM table.

previous Cake (µs) | new (µs) | vs det | vs non-Cake | new - previous
(µs) | pairs (new < prev / new > prev) | A/B |

The kernel's other Cake variants are the deterministic package
(`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_det_train`, `deterministic=True`)
and, in this package, the `fwd` and `fwd_short` forwards plus the
BF16-dw and FP32-dw backwards in short and long forms; they ship on
sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a, but sm_107a does not route `fwd_short` or
the short backwards.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**

* **Documentation**

across supported GPU architectures and thread usage.
* Clarified backward shared-memory requirements for non-deterministic
operation on R200 and B200 GPUs.

Co-authored-by: Yingyi Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [c8a473b](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c8a473b6a9ade35c614065f4ea0cc1edefa39f4d)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T14:07:44Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_causal_conv1d): reuse the non-deterministic single-rank launch plan per call row; coalesced FP64 flush on sm_103a bias + FP32-gradient backward (#8323)

The Cake causal conv1d training kernel (autograd forward + backward,
non-deterministic package
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_causal_conv1d_train_backend`) has
five single-rank routes and three context-parallel (KCP) forms. The
single-rank routes are default `bwd`, FP32 SiLU-gradient, FP32 bias,
BF16 dt-bias and fused bias + FP32-gradient. This PR changes only the
single-rank routes. Before this PR, every call re-ran route selection,
channel split, tile-override lookup and grid sizing, which cost several
microseconds of host time. Now forward and backward build a plan for
each call row (architecture, route, channel count, device, grid
multiple) once and reuse it. Launched programs and grids are unchanged.
On sm_103a, the fused bias + FP32-gradient backward now uses the
coalesced FP64 accumulator flush (backward main/new 1.006–1.010 at C ≥
1160). Over all shapes, the forward+backward step geomean is:

- 3.055× (GB300) and 3.255× (B200) faster than the fastest non-Cake SOTA
- 1.031× and 1.014× faster than deterministic Cake
- 1.006× and 1.003× faster than main, up to 1.070× and 1.071× at small
C, where the step is host-bound

**Geomean over all shapes, per GPU and phase, with [min, max] over
shapes** (GB300 / sm_103a: 90 shapes per phase; B200 / sm_100a: 72
shapes per phase). Ratios are baseline time / this PR's time, so above 1
means this PR is faster. All baselines are timed in the same processes:

- **det:** deterministic Cake
(`flashinfer.cake_causal_conv1d_det_train`) at the same FlashInfer main.
- **SOTA:** per shape, the fastest of fla 0.6.0 (`fla`, `fla_gluon`),
causal-conv1d 1.7.0 (`dao`, `dao_det`) and cuDNN frontend 1.32.1 that
runs every pass.
- **main:** FlashInfer main before this PR, which contains #8257.

Forward, backward and step are timed with CUPTI with a cold L2. The
checkpointed step (2× forward + backward) is timed with CUDA events.
Each value is the median of 8 passes per arm (16 for fused bias +
FP32-gradient on GB300), with palindromic order, per-process heap-layout
randomization and 3 rounds per pass. Software: CUDA 13.0 runtime,
PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130.

The PR comments have per-phase tables (forward, backward, step,
checkpointed step) with [min, max] for every shape.

The KCP contiguous, zigzag and zigzag-per-document forms are unchanged,
and the package ships on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

**R200 (sm_107a, 212 SMs), direction only.** This PR changes no sm_107a
device code. Same protocol, 8 passes per arm, 90 shapes per phase; the
SOTA column is the fastest of fla and causal-conv1d (cuDNN frontend does
not run on sm_107a). These rows come from a 212-SM part and show
direction only.

On R200, 92 of the 270 bwd, step and ckpt rows are below det Cake. The
worst is the FP32-gradient route at S = 250,340, C = 1024, bwd: det
154.8 µs, new 161.0 µs (0.961). FlashInfer main is below det Cake on 91
of the same rows, so these rows come from the current non-deterministic
kernels on this part, not from this PR. The per-shape tables are in the
comments below.

Co-authored-by: Yingyi Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [04ff9cc](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/04ff9ccf10230b1318489db06b403c639fa83930)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T13:56:04Z
- **提交信息**: feat(cake_gdn_kcp): with grad, in-kernel Q/K L2 norm for the non-deterministic KCP package (#7817) (#8316)

Cake ships four GDN (gated delta net) training packages in FlashInfer: a
deterministic and a non-deterministic package, each in a key-sharded
context-parallel (KCP) form and a single-rank form. All four take BF16 q
/ k / v with head dim 128 and, with this PR, accept the in-kernel Q / K
L2 normalization option `use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel`. This PR adds that
option to the non-deterministic KCP package
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_train_kcp` (layouts contiguous, zigzag
and zigzag per document), with the same contract as the deterministic
KCP package, which gained it in #8252. The facade
`flashinfer.cake_gdn_train_kcp` selects between the two KCP packages
with `deterministic=True` / `False`.

Against the deterministic KCP package, the non-deterministic package's
speedup on the claimed cells is:

- B200: 0.997 - 1.014
- GB300, layouts zigzag per document and zigzag: 0.996 - 1.022
- R200 CP4: 0.996 - 1.003
- R200 CP8, layouts contiguous and zigzag per document: 0.995 - 1.011
- R200 CP8 zigzag: slower on the forward (0.938), ckpt (0.954) and ckpt
with recompute handle (0.985), and faster on the backward (1.072) and
forward+backward (1.017).

Against the strongest non-Cake implementation:

- FlashQLA 0.1.3 dual-CP is faster on the forward on B200 (0.856 zigzag
per document, 0.819 zigzag) and on GB300 (0.872 zigzag per document,
0.803 zigzag).
- On those two GPUs, the non-deterministic package is faster on the
backward, forward+backward and ckpt (B200 1.267 - 1.565, GB300 1.293 -
1.666, layouts zigzag per document and zigzag).
- On R200 it is faster on every operation against FROST head-parallel
(CP8 3.443 - 4.301, CP4 3.537 - 4.592).

### Timing

- Timed step: the KCP causal conv1d (10240 channels) followed by the GDN
layer, timed per rank with CUDA events. Each iteration counts the
slowest rank's time. Execution is eager (no CUDA graphs), with a warm
JIT cache and a 256 MiB L2 flush before every iteration.
- Cake rows and the non-Cake implementations measured in the same runs
(FROST and FLA head-parallel, FLA KCP): 10 warmup iterations, then 5
groups x 2 palindromic blocks x 12 samples per implementation. Each cell
is the median.
- Sustained protocol (rows marked so): 3 groups x 2 palindromic blocks x
300 samples, 20 warmup iterations, 5 s cool-down before each block.
- FlashQLA (with FLA 0.6.0 KCP as its accuracy reference): its own run,
with 10 warmup iterations and 5 groups x 4 palindromic blocks x 12
samples.
- Non-Cake implementations time their own convolution, partition and
communication inside the same boundary: FlashQLA and FLA KCP split the
tokens evenly in every layout, and head-parallel runs an all-to-all head
split around single-rank kernels. Their time does not depend on the Cake
layout, so one non-Cake value per operation serves all layout rows.
- Speedup vs X = X ms / non-deterministic ms, computed from the absolute
values in the row.
- "(paired m [lo, hi] OK)" gives the median and range of the per-group
ratios from the same run. OK means every compared implementation's drift
is <= 2 %; UNSTABLE means some implementation's drift is above 2 %.
"UNSTABLE (cross-run)" marks cells whose two runs disagree. UNSTABLE
cells are not claimed.
  - "unpaired" means the two values come from different runs.
- Operations: bwd = (fwd+bwd) - fwd, computed from medians. ckpt =
checkpointed 2 x forward + backward. The recompute-handle row is Cake
only.
- "power-capped" means 5 % or more of the samples ran under the GPU's
software power cap. Such cells are not claimed.
- Every implementation runs with in-kernel Q / K L2 normalization on raw
q / k, on the same documents and seed.
- Baselines:
- Deterministic Cake is the deterministic KCP package at FlashInfer main
e74a1677, which includes #8252.
- Strongest non-Cake is the lowest median per operation among the
non-Cake implementations that pass the accuracy check: rel-RMS <= 1e-2
and max-abs <= 2e-2 x max|ref| on every output and input gradient,
against the non-deterministic package. FlashQLA is judged against FLA
0.6.0 KCP instead.
- Candidates: FlashQLA 0.1.3 dual-CP, FLA 0.6.0 KCP, FLA 0.6.0
head-parallel, and FROST head-parallel (cuDNN frontend 1.32.1, default
chunk and chunk 64).

The contiguous-layout rows come from one sustained-protocol run (rows
marked so) on another B200 node of the same type. That run's software
power-cap shares (deterministic / non-deterministic) are fwd 0.0 / 0.0
%, fwd+bwd 10.0 / 10.4 %, ckpt 2.5 / 3.4 % and ckpt with handle 2.4 /
2.5 %. The contiguous fwd+bwd and bwd cells are therefore power-capped
and not claimed.

On the contiguous layout, the FlashQLA value comes from its own
short-protocol run on another node and is not claimed.

FROST is not available on sm_103a with `use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel`,
because cuDNN frontend 1.32.1 offers no gdn_frost plan for this graph.

The zigzag-per-document and zigzag layouts ran once, in run 1. The
contiguous layout ran twice on the same nodes (run 1, run 2). Between
the two runs:

- the measured Cake medians moved by up to 26 % (fwd, fwd+bwd, ckpt and
ckpt with handle);
- the derived bwd moved by up to 39 %;
- FLA 0.6.0 KCP and FLA 0.6.0 head-parallel moved by at most 1.9 %.

Both runs are shown, and no contiguous-layout number is claimed.

because the first run's drift was above 2 %. The re-measure ran on
another node of the same 212-SM class; its non-Cake column takes the
lowest median over both contiguous runs.

for this PR: no model-step harness was available for it, so no
model-step number is claimed for either package.

package `flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_det_train_kcp`, the
deterministic single-rank package
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_det_train` and the non-deterministic
single-rank package `flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_gdn_train`; all
four packages ship sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

### [ecb713c](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/ecb713c63c178e7fe195a38ece15e1eaa93804f5)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T13:43:59Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mega_moe_v3): faster TP8 T4096 rank program on sm_103a (#8327)

`flashinfer.experimental.mega_moe_v3` runs the Cake MegaMoE v3 prepared
pipeline for the 384-expert, top-6, hidden-5120 model with activation
clamp 10. A single kernel launch covers dispatch, FC1, clamped SwiGLU,
MXFP8 activation quantization, FC2 and weighted combine. The kernel has
four variants on main, and this PR updates one of them: the TP/EP rank
variant. It changes 1 of the variant's 32 programs, which is TP8 EP1
(384 experts) at 4096 tokens.

This program's activation load warp now keeps a shared-memory copy of
the expert row offsets. It reads each task's offset from this copy
instead of from global memory. Its host binding takes 1536 B more
dynamic shared memory (221696 B in total).

The routes and the other 31 rank programs are unchanged. The baseline is
the previous Cake version on main, which is the rank variant as last
updated by #8244. For replicates a / b, the speedups for the changed
program are:

- TP8 EP1 at 4096 tokens: 1.007x / 1.007x

That saves 2.09 / 2.08 µs per call. The change is faster than the A/A
noise band in both replicates. The unchanged rows run 0.9995x to 1.0014x
in replicate a and 0.9977x to 1.0017x in replicate b.

*NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs), CUDA 13.4, driver 580.159.03, PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130. Per-call latency comes from CUDA-graph replays (20 calls
per graph), taking the median of 21 in-process rounds. The previous
version and this PR ran in separate processes, alternating over 6
rounds. Each value is the median of the 6 process medians. Speedup =
previous / this PR. Columns a and b are two independent replicates, each
run alone on its own node. Each replicate also timed the previous
version against itself (an A/A control) to measure its noise band. The
widest band is 0.16 % in replicate a and 0.22 % in replicate b. The 31
unchanged programs have byte-identical kernels and host bindings. One of
them, TP8 EP8 at 16 tokens, reads slower than its band in both
replicates (+0.01 / +0.06 µs, speedup 0.9997 / 0.9985). This is
process-level noise, not a regression.*

The other three variants (single-rank routed-FP4, single-rank routed-FP8
and grouped-GEMM routes) ship on sm_100a and sm_103a; the rank variant
ships on sm_103a only.

### [2d50b55](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/2d50b554905ee30551abce2b8a8cbbcb7047a294)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T13:26:07Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mhc): with grad, GB300 column-slab PDL bands in the nd autograd route (#8304)

This PR adds GB300-specific launch bands for one edge of Cake's mHC
(manifold-constrained hyper-connections) training kernel. Cake's mHC
training kernel has a deterministic mode and an opt-in non-deterministic
mode, nd (`deterministic=False` of
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_mhc_train`). Some nd kernel launches
use programmatic dependent launch (PDL), which lets the dependent kernel
launch before its predecessor finishes. Per call, PDL is turned on or
off by token-count (T) bands, set per architecture, edge (predecessor ->
dependent kernel) and call path. #8281 added the nd package's own bands,
keyed by (architecture, SM count, hidden size), with B200 entries only.

The new GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs) entries cover the column slab of the
checkpointed backward (the column-slab pass after the backward fn split,
on the checkpoint path). Before this PR, GB300 used the deterministic
package's band there at every hidden size: PDL off for T = 4097..8192,
on elsewhere.
- **Column slab on GB300:** PDL is now off for
  - hidden 4096: T = 1152..2112 and 4097..8192;
  - hidden 5120: T = 1088..1920, 4097..8192 and from 24577 up;
  - hidden 7168: from T = 832 up.
- **Unchanged launches:** the forward, the backward from saved
statistics and the other GB300 edges. B200 and GB200 (sm_100a), B300
(sm_103a, 148 SMs) and sm_107a launch exactly as before.
- **Unchanged outputs:** PDL is a scheduling attribute, and the same
programs run on the same buffers.

**Speedup vs the previous nd version.** "new" is nd with this PR.
"previous" is the same build with the nd package's own bands removed. On
GB300 that is exactly how nd launched before this PR, including with
#8281. The table lists only the 45 rows where the two launch
differently, all checkpointed step (5 at hidden 4096, 13 at 5120, 27 at
7168). The forward and the backward launch identically, so they are not
listed.

How the first table was timed:
- All arms run in one process on the same inputs, in ABBA (mirrored)
order inside each group.
- Each arm replays a CUDA graph of the checkpointed step after a 512 MiB
L2 flush.
- Latency is the median over 16 groups of the per-group mean of 30
replays.
- "previous" is timed in two arms. The table shows the first arm, and
the gap between the two arms is the null.
- Speedup = previous / new. Above 1 means new is faster.
- Compare ratios within a table. This timing differs from the
two-baseline tables.

This branch was merged with FlashInfer main, without a rebase. The first
table's hidden 4096 rows were measured on this PR's second commit,
before the merge. Its hidden 5120 and 7168 rows were measured on the
first commit. The second commit only moves the start of the hidden 4096
band from 1025 to 1152, so those rows run the same launches as the
second commit. The merge does not change the launches this table
compares. The two-baseline tables were measured on the merged head.

40 rows are faster, 5 are at parity and none is slower:
- hidden 7168: at T <= 4096 the rows read 1.000 to 1.029 (0.02 to 6.81
us faster). Above 4096 they read 1.003 to 1.010 (4.83 to 34.11 us
faster).
- hidden 5120: at T <= 1920 the rows read 1.000 to 1.033 (up to 6.95 us
faster). Above 24576 they read 1.000 to 1.002 (0.38 to 8.75 us faster).
- hidden 4096: the rows read 1.004 to 1.021 (0.81 to 3.19 us faster),
with new faster in 15 or 16 of 16 groups.

The parity rows:
- hidden 7168 T = 832: 1.000, 8 of 16, null 0.03 us;
- hidden 5120 T = 1088: 1.001, 10 of 16, null 0.19 us;
- hidden 5120 T = 1150: 1.000 (new 0.07 us slower), 8 of 16, null 0.90
us;
- hidden 5120 T = 28672: 1.000, 9 of 16, null 0.02 us;
- hidden 4096 T = 1535: 1.011, 16 of 16, but its null (2.12 us) is
larger than the 1.62 us gain.

In earlier runs of the same comparison, hidden 7168 T = 832 read 0.53 us
faster (13 of 16). Hidden 5120 T = 1088 and 1150 read 1.61 to 4.31 us
faster (15 or 16 of 16).

The hidden 4096 band starts at 1152. From 1025 to 1151 tokens, PDL off
was faster in one run and slower in another (up to 0.75 us slower, 0 of
16 at T = 1088). So those token counts keep PDL on.

NVIDIA GB300, sm_103a (152 SMs). Cake kernels: CUDA 13.4 toolkit, driver
580.159.03. X BF16 [T, 4, H], FP32 mapping, 4 streams, non-KCP.
CUDA-graph replay after a 512 MiB L2 flush, median of 16 ABBA groups x
30 replays. "previous" is the first of two arms.

**Baselines and method** for the two-baseline tables (one per hidden
size, T = 256 to 65536). They have 29 token counts at hidden 4096 and 32
at 5120 and 7168. That is the 27 token counts of #8281's tables plus
token counts in and around the new bands.
- **det:** the deterministic mode (`deterministic=True`) from the same
build: FlashInfer main merged into this PR, including #8256 and #8266.
It is the original deterministic Cake implementation, and this PR does
not change it. #8266 adds an sm_100a column-slab program and does not
affect GB300.
- **det2:** a second det call timed in the same groups. A row is within
its own noise when it is below 1.000 vs det by at most its own |det2/det
- 1| (unrounded).
- **B0 (non-Cake SOTA):** per row, the faster of IEEE-FP32 eager PyTorch
and `torch.compile(fullgraph=False, dynamic=False)` of the same mHC
training function, with TF32 off. `torch.compile` won on every row, and
the parenthesis in the B0 column names the winner.
- **Why B0:** B0 is the strongest applicable baseline because it is the
only non-Cake implementation of this function at these sizes.
TransformerEngine's mHC (TF32 mapping math, log-domain Sinkhorn without
eps) and Megatron-LM's fused mHC (TF32 projection) compute a different
function. FlashInfer's `flashinfer.mhc` kernels and DeepGEMM's mega_mhc
are inference only.
- **Operations:** forward = forward prepare + forward finish. Backward =
backward prepare + backward finish from saved statistics. Checkpointed
step = forward + statistics recompute (`cake_mhc_train_forward_stats`) +
backward on the checkpoint path. For B0, the checkpointed step is a
no-grad forward + a with-grad forward + the backward.
- **Workload:** X BF16 [T, 4, H], FP32 mapping, 4 streams, non-KCP,
random inputs.
- **Speedup:** det or B0 latency / new latency. Above 1 means new is
faster.
- **Comparability:** on every row, the new forward outputs, dX and the
other backward outputs except dfn, dscale and dbase are bitwise equal to
det. dscale and dbase are bitwise equal to det at hidden 5120 and 7168,
and at hidden 4096 for T up to 8192. At hidden 4096 from T = 14928 (10
token counts), det now sums their terms in another fixed order, #8256's
group-row order. nd does not copy that order, so their last bits can
differ there. The new dfn relative L2 vs det is at most 8.71e-08 /
8.73e-08 / 8.67e-08 at hidden 4096 / 5120 / 7168. B0's dfn relative L2
vs det is at most 4.74e-06 / 4.83e-06 / 5.00e-06.

**Speedup vs det and B0.** Geomean speedups over each table's token
counts (forward / backward / checkpointed step):

| hidden | vs det | vs B0 |
|---|---|---|
| 4096 | 1.001 / 1.069 / 1.038 | 11.17 / 8.90 / 12.57 |
| 5120 | 1.000 / 1.080 / 1.040 | 12.86 / 8.76 / 13.60 |
| 7168 | 1.000 / 1.044 / 1.025 | 13.64 / 8.60 / 14.14 |

No row is slower than B0. The smallest speedup vs B0 is 6.76 (hidden
4096 forward, T = 256).

nd and det run the same forward launches on GB300, so forward rows near
1.000 are noise. The forward det null spread (max |det2/det - 1|) is
0.17 % / 0.22 % / 0.25 % at hidden 4096 / 5120 / 7168.

Two checkpointed-step rows are below 1.000 vs det, both at hidden 5120.
As (speedup vs det, det2/det), they are T = 32768 (0.996, 1.000) and T =
65536 (0.990, 1.000). Neither is within its own noise. Hidden 4096 and
7168 have none, and no backward row is below 1.000. These two token
counts are inside the new bands. In the first table, this PR makes them
faster than before: hidden 5120 T = 32768 reads 1.0006 and 65536 reads
1.0017. So the remaining gap to det at these sizes was already there
before this PR. Earlier GB300 measurements, taken before this PR, put
the hidden 5120 T = 65536 checkpointed step at 0.991 vs det.

### [958178d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/958178d3a3ef2a5cebee655a91a0f811a32cf600)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T13:24:13Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_gemm): router weight gradient tables for 208-SM and 212-SM sm_107a parts (#8310)

## Summary

`flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_gemm` provides two kinds of
GEMM. The first is BF16-input dense and batched projection GEMMs with
BF16 or FP32 weight-gradient output. The second is an FP32 router GEMM
with 256 experts and BF16x3 emulation. A keyword-only `deterministic`
flag selects the variant: `deterministic=True` (the default) calls
`flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_det_gemm`.
`deterministic=False` runs the split-K, stream-K and head/tail programs
of #8190, #8238 and #8261.

This PR changes only the planner table. It does not change a kernel. The
change applies to the router weight gradient with `deterministic=False`
on R200 (`sm_107a`) parts with 208 or 212 SMs. At hidden 5120 and 16172
<= T <= 16384, these parts now run the head/tail program
`router_fp32_gemm_atomic_nn_t_ht_c3_nreg` (#8238) with the "H0.5x4"
partition: 520 units (52 head spans) on 208 SMs and 530 units (53 head
spans) on 212 SMs. #8261 runs the deterministic six-split program there,
because its head/tail window holds only on 216 SMs. All other plans and
`deterministic=True` are unchanged.

The table gives the geomean (min-max) of the per-row ratios for each SM
count and op; the full rows follow the legend. No wgrad, bwd or 2fwd+bwd
row is slower than either baseline. (#8261 / FI main)/new equals det
Cake/new on every row.

| SMs (parts) | op | rows | det/new = (#8261 / FI main)/new, geomean
(range) | SOTA/new, geomean (range) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 212 (1-4) | wgrad | 48 | 1.231 (1.186-1.252) | 1.689 (1.648-1.729) |
| 212 (1-4) | bwd | 48 | 1.105 (1.083-1.137) | 1.385 (1.345-1.436) |
| 212 (1-4) | 2fwd+bwd | 48 | 1.058 (1.040-1.088) | 1.722 (1.667-1.787)
|
| 208 (1, 2) | wgrad | 24 | 1.215 (1.204-1.226) | 1.672 (1.639-1.700) |
| 208 (3) | wgrad | 12 | 1.065 (1.043-1.075) | 1.743 (1.681-1.768) |
| 208 (1, 2) | bwd | 24 | 1.102 (1.075-1.160) | 1.405 (1.355-1.465) |
| 208 (3) | bwd | 12 | 1.030 (1.027-1.032) | 1.381 (1.358-1.397) |
| 208 (1, 2) | 2fwd+bwd | 24 | 1.056 (1.046-1.065) | 1.739 (1.660-1.765)
|
| 208 (3) | 2fwd+bwd | 12 | 1.008 (1.006-1.009) | 1.690 (1.657-1.714) |

*Table: geomean (min-max) of the per-row ratios. R200 (`sm_107a`), CUDA
13.4. 208-SM part 3 ran at a lower SM clock.*

This PR does not change the forward. Every Cake arm (det Cake, #8261 /
FI main, new) runs the same forward program, so forward det/new is
parity within noise. The table gives, per SM count, the absolute forward
latency ranges and the unpaired and paired det/new ranges.

| SMs (parts) | fwd rows | det Cake us | new us | SOTA us | det/new,
unpaired | det/new, paired | SOTA/new |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 212 (1-4) | 48 | 116.4-132.2 | 116.7-131.4 | 246.8-264.1 | 0.979-1.014
| 0.992-1.004 | 1.992-2.130 |
| 208 (1, 2) | 24 | 120.2-136.4 | 119.8-135.7 | 257.9-278.8 |
0.955-1.043 | 0.995-1.009 | 2.029-2.168 |
| 208 (3) | 12 | 172.8-178.1 | 173.3-178.2 | 351.0-356.9 | 0.996-1.001 |
0.996-1.001 | 1.971-2.043 |

*Table: forward ranges over the rows of each SM count. Paired det/new: 1
/ median over the 9 paired groups of new/det. R200 (`sm_107a`), CUDA
13.4.*

Unpaired whole-op ratios (det/new of the cell medians) carry about
+/-4.5 % noise on 208-SM part 1, as the identical forward program shows
(unpaired 0.955-1.043, paired 0.995-1.004), so the paired values are the
reliable comparison.

**Legend**

- Row: one part, process, T (16172, 16231, 16384), mode and op. There
are 336 rows: 7 parts x 2 processes x 3 T x 2 modes x 4 ops.
- Latency: median us of the CUPTI GPU span, from the first kernel start
to the last kernel end. The span includes all launches of the op. Each
iteration starts with a cold L2 (a write of twice the L2 size). Arms
rotate in each paired group. wgrad uses 15 groups x 20 steps. fwd, bwd
and 2fwd+bwd use 9 groups. Each cell is the median of the group medians.
- det Cake: `deterministic=True`. #8261 / FI main: the previous Cake
version, #8261 (0f78e254) and FI main at this PR's base (e74a1677). Both
run the same program here, so this column repeats det Cake. SOTA:
`cublasSgemm_v2` with `CUBLAS_FP32_EMULATED_BF16X9_MATH` for every GEMM.
TF32 and BF16 miss the router's FP32 accuracy budget, so SOTA is the
strongest applicable call.
- Ratio: baseline us / new us. A value above 1.00 means this PR is
faster.
- fwd: forward. wgrad: weight gradient, FP32 [256, 5120]. bwd: input
gradient + wgrad. 2fwd+bwd: 2 x forward + bwd. Cake arms share the
forward and input-gradient programs. e = eager, g = CUDA graph.
- Process A: one process for all rows. Process B: a new process per row,
in reverse order.
- R200 `sm_107a`; driver 620.62 (212 SMs), 615.71.10 (208 SMs); CUDA
13.4 (nvcc 13.4.92); PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130; cuBLAS 13.8.0.4.
- The GPUs of 212-SM parts 1-4 and 208-SM parts 1-2 briefly hit the
software power cap (4 to 15 nvidia-smi samples each). 208-SM part 3 ran
at a 1992 MHz median SM clock, against 2424 MHz on parts 1 and 2, and
hit the power cap in 38-46 % of its samples. Its gains are smaller.

### [f00ee26](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/f00ee26b15219d141ffb98d68677bb5439b39098)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T13:06:05Z
- **提交信息**: feat(cake_lm_head_det_loss): sm_107a (R200) record with every sm_103a program (#8260)

The deterministic chunked LM-head + loss training backend
(`flashinfer.chunked_lm_head`, BF16 X [T, H], W [V, H]) has five Cake
variants, and this PR delivers the sm_107a (R200) build of the whole
family, with every kernel stage the sm_103a build has, for #7636. There
is no earlier Cake sm_107a build, so each row compares against the
fastest non-Cake implementation measured for that objective on the same
GPU and inputs (H = 6144, V = 154880). Latency is forward + backward per
training step. Cake is 1.02-1.52x faster than Liger 0.8.5 fused linear
cross-entropy on the "ce" loss (close to parity at T=32463), 2.02-2.21x
faster than PyTorch 2.14.1 chunked on the policy loss and 1.59-1.78x
faster than PyTorch 2.14.1 unchunked on log-prob; Liger has no policy or
log-prob objective.

Table. NVIDIA R200 (212 SMs), sm_107a, CUDA 13.4.92.

### [b120e42](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/b120e4217c39d1794cb65374449e578bb043fc96)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T12:53:46Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_tinygemm2_wgmma): sm_90a routing windows extended between grid values (#8324)

`tinygemm_bf16` has four variants: with or without bias, each with or
without programmatic dependent launch (PDL). This PR changes only the
host routing of the sm_90a wgmma programs (`cake_tinygemm2_wgmma`) for
all four variants. The programs themselves are unchanged from #8306. The
H100 routing windows now also cover shapes between the measured grid
values (9 batches, 7 output and 8 input feature counts). A window
extends between two grid values only where every grid shape around it
and every shape re-measured inside it was at least 3% faster than
`csrc/tinygemm2.cu` and bit-identical. 7342 between-grid shapes were
re-measured; a tile measured below 3% at any of them is not routed in
that region. Over the grid shapes plus the between-grid test shapes
(9044 shape/bias combinations), 8111 now take a generated program, up
from 5759 with #8306. The 1008 grid shapes route exactly as in #8306
(983 routed). Shapes outside the windows keep the mma.sync reference
`csrc/tinygemm2.cu`. Every row in both tables below is bit-identical to
`csrc/tinygemm2.cu` and faster than it in every one of the 7 rounds. The
median speedup is 1.027x to 4.324x with PDL off and 1.026x to 4.323x
with PDL on. Rows marked "(reference)" in the #8306 column are shapes
that the previous Cake routing of #8306 left on `csrc/tinygemm2.cu`.
They now take a generated program, at 1.056x (3x1536x2560 without bias)
to 3.665x (40x4096x7168 without bias) with PDL off, and 1.056x
(3x1536x2560 without bias) to 3.660x (40x4096x7168 with bias) with PDL
on. One shape changes its program: 2x2048x3072 without bias moves from
PACKED_U4_IL_BOX3D to PACKED_S8_IL_BOX3D, going from 7.968 us to 7.904
us (1.008x) with PDL both off and on. Rows marked "(unchanged)" run the
same program as #8306. Their "Speedup vs #8306" values, which range from
0.995 to 1.034, are measurement noise between identical code and not
improvements.

*NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3, sm_90a, CUDA 13.4 toolkit (torch 2.14.1+cu130).
Median CUPTI kernel time, cold L2, 7 interleaved rounds x 200
iterations. The three arms (`csrc/tinygemm2.cu`, the #8306 routing and
programs, this PR) were measured in the same process on the same GPU,
and every output is bit-identical to `csrc/tinygemm2.cu`. "Program" is
the program this PR routes the shape to.*

### [473993f](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/473993f4eb44bc0558c511d7a9444afae2a2a536)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T12:47:47Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_moe_finalize_allreduce_fusion): two-shot early programs for batches of up to 128 tokens at world sizes 4 and 8 (#8321)

This PR adds 8 two-shot early programs to
`cake_moe_finalize_allreduce_fusion` (2 data types x 2 epilogues x world
sizes 4 and 8). A two-shot early program runs the same exchange as the
two-shot program. The difference is that it issues the first token's
routing-index loads without waiting for the load of the all-reduce
control words, so those loads no longer depend on the control-word load.
A two-shot batch of at most 128 tokens now runs the two-shot early
program. Larger batches run the two-shot and deferred two-shot programs
as before. With the default `small_token_max` of 64, this covers 72 to
128 tokens at world size 4 and 56 to 128 tokens at world size 8. With a
smaller `small_token_max`, world size 8 also runs the two-shot early
program from `small_token_max + 1` tokens. World size 2 does not change.

The kernel fuses MoE finalize, the all-reduce across the ranks of one
NVLink node, the residual add and RMSNorm at hidden size 7168. MoE
finalize uses the top-k expert rows with their routing scale, plus an
optional shared-expert row. The kernel is called through
`flashinfer.comm.allreduce_fusion(..., moe_finalize_backend="cake")`. It
has no other Cake variants: it ships only in this fused form and covers
sm_100a and sm_103a. With this PR it has 48 programs per architecture
(40 before): 2 data types (fp16, bf16) x 2 epilogues (BF16/FP16 output,
packed NVFP4 output) x 12 program kinds. World size 2 has small-token,
persistent and large-token programs. World size 4 has small-token,
persistent, two-shot, two-shot early and deferred two-shot programs.
World size 8 has small-token, two-shot, two-shot early and deferred
two-shot programs.

The baseline is the previous Cake version on FlashInfer main (PR #8139).
In the table, this PR changes the program of the 64 shapes with 128
tokens at world sizes 4 and 8. Their geomean speedup is 1.039x on B300
(min 1.010x, max 1.079x) and 1.038x on B200 (min 1.006x, max 1.080x).
The other 656 shapes run the same program on both sides. Their geomean
is 0.999x on B300 (min 0.971x, max 1.031x) and 0.999x on B200 (min
0.985x, max 1.015x). Over all 720 shapes of the table, the geomean is
1.003x on B300 and 1.003x on B200.

The measurement also covers all 320 shapes whose program this PR
changes; the 64 changed shapes in the table are among them. They are 72,
88, 95, 96, 104 and 128 tokens at world size 4; 64, 65, 72 and 128
tokens at world size 8, each with 32 combinations of dtype, top-k, PDL,
NVFP4 output and shared expert. On those 320 shapes, the geomean speedup
is 1.036x on B300 (min 1.010x) and 1.035x on B200 (min 1.006x). None of
them measures below 1.000 on either GPU.

The tables below give one row per shape of the owner shape list. They
were measured on NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (sm_103a) and NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a)
with CUDA 13.4 and the default `small_token_max` of 64. The previous and
this-PR columns are the median CUPTI kernel time in microseconds, taking
the minimum over ranks. Speedup is the median of paired previous/this-PR
ratios from interleaved runs, with its 95% bootstrap confidence
interval. For this reason, a few rows with bimodal timing show a speedup
that differs from the ratio of the two median times. Values above 1 mean
this PR is faster. In the flag columns (PDL, NVFP4 out, shared expert),
1 means yes and 0 means no.

## Summary

`test_gpu_k1_row_major_program` (added in #8275) required the 192-wide
row-major weight-gradient program on every Blackwell part. The package
registers that program on `sm_107a` only, so the test failed on
`sm_100a` and `sm_103a` with "dense_proj_gemm_atomic_nn_n192_f32 is not
registered" instead of skipping. The test now skips on parts other than
`sm_107a` and still requires the program on `sm_107a`. Test-only change;
no package code changes.

### [3b2d966](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/3b2d9661c9754352d15fed8bb6b7ab77e9071bbd)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T11:48:00Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mhc): with grad, B200 PDL bands in the nd training route (#8281)

Cake's mHC (manifold-constrained hyper-connections) training kernel has
a deterministic mode and an opt-in non-deterministic mode, nd
(`deterministic=False` of
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_mhc_train`). Some nd kernel launches
use programmatic dependent launch (PDL), which lets the dependent kernel
launch before its predecessor finishes. Per call, PDL is turned on or
off by token-count (T) bands. The bands are set per architecture, edge
(predecessor -> dependent kernel) and call path. Before this PR, nd used
the deterministic package's bands on every GPU.

This PR adds the nd package's own bands, keyed by (architecture, SM
count, hidden size). It also passes the device SM count when the route
is planned. Only B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs) gets bands of its own:
- **Forward collapse and backward prepare:** the forward collapse
(forward) and the backward prepare of the checkpointed backward turn PDL
off for T = 2945..3456, in addition to the existing 4097..8192. In that
range the mapping pass runs 24 to 27 token tiles, and with PDL on the
dependent kernel stalls.
- **Column slab:** the column slab of the checkpointed backward gets
bands per hidden size. PDL is off for T = 1025..2048 and 4097..8192 at
hidden 4096, 1025..2047 at 5120 and 897..8192 at 7168. Before this PR,
all three were off for 1025..8192.
- **Unchanged launches:** the backward from saved statistics is
unchanged. GB200 (sm_100a, 152 SMs), GB300 and B300 (sm_103a) and
sm_107a launch exactly as before.
- **Unchanged outputs:** PDL is a scheduling attribute, and the same
programs run on the same buffers.

**Speedup vs the previous nd version.** "new" is nd with this PR.
"previous" is the same build with the nd package's own bands removed,
which is how nd launched before this PR. The table lists only the 43
rows where the two launch differently (15 forward, 28 checkpointed
step). The backward rows launch identically, so they are not listed.

How the first table was timed:
- All arms run in one process on the same inputs, in ABBA (mirrored)
order inside each group.
- Each arm replays a CUDA graph of the forward or the checkpointed step
after a 512 MiB L2 flush.
- Latency is the median over 16 groups of the per-group mean of 30
replays.
- "previous" is timed in two arms. The table shows the first arm, and
the gap between the two arms is the null.
- "groups new faster" counts the groups (of 16) where new is faster.
- Speedup = previous / new. Above 1 means new is faster.

This timing differs from the two-baseline tables, so compare ratios
within a table, not absolute latencies across tables.

The first table and the hidden 7168 two-baseline rows were measured on
this PR's first commit; the hidden 4096 and 5120 two-baseline rows on
its head. The second commit only moves the lower bound of the hidden
7168 column-slab band from 705 to 897 tokens. No measured token count
lies in 705..896, so every row runs the same launches as the head.

The forward rows (T = 2945..3456 at each hidden size) read 1.029 to
1.041, with new faster in 16 of 16 groups. The checkpointed-step rows at
T = 2945..3456 read 1.051 to 1.059 (13.4 to 27.1 us faster), also 16 of
16. The other checkpointed-step rows come from the column-slab bands.
They read 1.000 to 1.007, except hidden 5120 T = 3584 (0.998).

Three rows have new faster in fewer than 12 of 16 groups:
- hidden 4096 T = 3584 checkpointed step: 1.000, 11 of 16, new -
previous = -0.04 us, null 0.06 us;
- hidden 4096 T = 4096 checkpointed step: 1.000, 6 of 16, new - previous
= -0.03 us, null 0.04 us;
- hidden 5120 T = 3584 checkpointed step: 0.998, 1 of 16, new 0.56 us
slower, null 0.17 us.

The first two are within their null. The third is a small loss on this
run. Other runs of the same comparison at that token count read:
- 0.235 us faster (11 of 16);
- 0.217 us slower (2 of 16);
- 0.051 us faster (9 of 16).

A sweep of 21 token counts from 3457 to 4096 at hidden 5120 had 14
faster, 6 parity and 1 slower (+0.11 us at 3553). So the band stays.

NVIDIA B200, sm_100a (148 SMs). Cake kernels: CUDA 13.4 toolkit, driver
580.82.07. X BF16 [T, 4, H], FP32 mapping, 4 streams, non-KCP.
CUDA-graph replay after a 512 MiB L2 flush, median of 16 ABBA groups x
30 replays. "previous" is the first of two arms.

**Baselines and method** for the two-baseline tables (one per hidden
size, 27 token counts each, T = 256 to 65536):
- **det:** the deterministic mode (`deterministic=True`) from the same
build. It is the original deterministic Cake implementation, and this PR
does not change it.
- **det2:** a second det call timed in the same groups. A row is within
its own noise when it is below 1.000 vs det by at most its own |det2/det
- 1| (unrounded).
- **B0 (non-Cake SOTA):** per row, the faster of IEEE-FP32 eager PyTorch
and `torch.compile(fullgraph=False, dynamic=False)` of the same mHC
training function, with TF32 off. `torch.compile` won on every row, and
the parenthesis in the B0 column names the winner.
- **Why B0:** B0 is the strongest applicable baseline because it is the
only non-Cake implementation of this function at these sizes.
TransformerEngine's mHC (TF32 mapping math, log-domain Sinkhorn without
eps) and Megatron-LM's fused mHC (TF32 projection) compute a different
function. FlashInfer's `flashinfer.mhc` kernels and DeepGEMM's mega_mhc
are inference only.
- **Operations:** forward = forward prepare + forward finish. Backward =
backward prepare + backward finish from saved statistics. Checkpointed
step = forward + statistics recompute (`cake_mhc_train_forward_stats`) +
backward on the checkpoint path. For B0, the checkpointed step is a
no-grad forward + a with-grad forward + the backward.
- **Workload:** X BF16 [T, 4, H], FP32 mapping, 4 streams, non-KCP,
random inputs.
- **Speedup:** det or B0 latency / new latency. Above 1 means new is
faster.
- **Comparability:** on every row, all new outputs except dfn are
bitwise equal to det. The new dfn relative L2 vs det is at most 9.42e-08
/ 9.63e-08 / 9.74e-08 at hidden 4096 / 5120 / 7168. B0's dfn relative L2
vs det is at most 4.76e-06 / 4.81e-06 / 5.06e-06.

**Speedup vs det and B0.** Geomean speedups over the 27 token counts
(forward / backward / checkpointed step):

| hidden | vs det | vs B0 |
|---|---|---|
| 4096 | 1.000 / 1.050 / 1.026 | 11.83 / 8.82 / 12.78 |
| 5120 | 1.002 / 1.044 / 1.026 | 13.20 / 8.77 / 13.67 |
| 7168 | 1.006 / 1.027 / 1.025 | 14.36 / 8.51 / 14.22 |

No row is slower than B0. The smallest speedup vs B0 is 7.03 (hidden
4096 forward, T = 256).

Outside T = 2945..3456, nd and det run the same forward launches, so
forward rows near 1.000 are noise. The forward det null spread (max
|det2/det - 1|) is 0.23 % / 0.27 % / 0.65 % at hidden 4096 / 5120 /
7168. In eager timing, the in-band forward stall shows in two places:
- at hidden 7168, T = 2976..3456 read 1.039 to 1.042;
- at T = 3072 for hidden 4096 and 5120, both read 1.036.

The other in-band forward rows at hidden 4096 / 5120 read 0.997 to
1.003.

The backward and checkpointed-step rows below 1.000 vs det are listed
below as (speedup vs det, det2/det). Rows not marked as within their own
noise are below 1.000 by more than their own |det2/det - 1|.
- hidden 4096: checkpointed step T = 512 (0.998, 0.999). No backward row
is below 1.000; the smallest is 1.004 (T = 16263).
- hidden 5120:
  - checkpointed step T = 256 (0.996, 1.000) and 512 (0.998, 1.000);
- within their own noise: backward T = 15288 (0.985, 1.019), 16114
(0.998, 1.012) and 65536 (0.993, 1.018).
- hidden 7168:
  - backward T = 14928 (0.992, 0.997) and 65536 (0.999, 1.001);
- checkpointed step T = 14928 (0.997, 1.002), 16164 (0.990, 1.007) and
32768 (0.996, 0.998);
- within their own noise: backward T = 16164 (0.992, 1.010) and 32768
(0.981, 1.033), and checkpointed step T = 15288 (0.990, 1.022) and 15566
(0.994, 1.019).

None of these token counts is inside a band this PR changes (all are
below 1024 or above 8192), so this PR does not move them. They are the
existing nd vs det gap in eager timing.

### [bca46b9](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/bca46b9b018c2926b06d335e77aa7e62ec4dd3de)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T11:42:01Z
- **提交信息**: feat(cake_lm_head_det_loss): scalar and per-token temperature for chunked_lm_head_det_logprob (#8254)

The deterministic chunked LM-head + loss training backend
(`flashinfer.chunked_lm_head`) has five Cake variants. This PR adds
scalar and per-token temperature to `chunked_lm_head_det_logprob`, in
both the forward and backward passes, with temperature-aware gradients.
The baseline is PyTorch eager `log_softmax(X @ W^T / tau)` with
autograd, gathering the label log-probability, using the same per-token
temperature tensor and identical BF16 inputs (H = 6144, V = 154880).
Measuring forward + backward per step across the measured rows, Cake is
1.38-1.54x faster on B200 and 1.46-1.64x faster on GB300. On B200 at
T=65031, eager runs out of memory. For #7637.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* Deterministic selected-token log-probability calls now support scalar
and per-token temperatures, with temperature-aware gradients.
  * Preloading can include temperature-enabled computation paths.
* Benchmarks can compare temperature configurations and include a Cake
log-probability run.
* **Bug Fixes**
* Unsupported temperature combinations now raise clear validation
errors, including temperature use with non-deterministic calls or
keep-logits memory mode.
* **Documentation**
* Added guidance on temperature inputs, validation, numerical behavior,
gradient handling, and preload requirements.

### [d90f65b](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/d90f65b9ea9d3495faeccc5ef51381de1f1dd79e)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T11:41:28Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_tinygemm2_wgmma): sm_90a packed and accumulator ring fill reordered, interleaved packed tiles, re-measured routing (#8306)

`tinygemm_bf16` has four variants: with or without bias, each with or
without programmatic dependent launch (PDL). This PR updates the sm_90a
wgmma programs (`cake_tinygemm2_wgmma`) for all four variants. The
packed and accumulator programs issue their first pipeline stage sooner
and, with PDL, issue no copy before the grid-dependency wait. Two new
packed tiles, PACKED_U4_IL and PACKED_S8_IL, use an interleaved copy
order that is faster at some shapes. The H100 routing windows are
re-measured, and the cluster programs are unchanged. With the new
windows, 983 of the 1008 measured H100 grid shapes take a generated
program, up from 903 in #8232. Shapes outside the windows keep the
mma.sync reference `csrc/tinygemm2.cu`. Every row in both tables below
is faster than `csrc/tinygemm2.cu`, by 1.026x to 4.285x with PDL off and
1.027x to 4.289x with PDL on. 8x1024x1024 without bias, which #8232 left
on `csrc/tinygemm2.cu`, now takes PACKED_U4_BOX3D (1.027x). Compared
with the previous Cake programs of #8232, this PR is up to 1.070x faster
with PDL off and up to 1.076x faster with PDL on (64x4096x3072), and no
row is slower at the timer's 32 ns resolution. The lowest ratios print
as 1.000. The cluster rows run byte-identical programs, so their ratios
are measurement noise.

*NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3, sm_90a, CUDA 13.4 toolkit (torch 2.14.1+cu130).
Median CUPTI kernel time, cold L2, 7 interleaved rounds x 200
iterations. The three arms (`csrc/tinygemm2.cu`, the #8232 programs and
routing, this PR) were measured in the same process on the same GPU, and
every output is bit-identical to `csrc/tinygemm2.cu`. "Program" is the
program this PR routes the shape to.*

### [c4ae6c2](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c4ae6c2f808923dbb1deacc2c79b19b9763f876b)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T11:38:43Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kimi_k3_attn_res): faster programs for more B200, B300 and GB300 shapes (#8291)

This PR changes routes of the Cake AttnRes operator,
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_kimi_k3_attn_res`, which is exposed as
`flashinfer.kimi_k3_attn_res.prepare_kimi_k3_attn_res` and
`kimi_k3_attn_res`. One launch does residual add, an optional snapshot
write, K+1 candidate scoring, softmax, mix and output RMSNorm. It takes
BF16 inputs with hidden size 7168 and K in [0, 8]. It has one data type,
one layout and two fused forms: dense and snapshot write. This PR
changes routes on B200, B300 and GB300 at both PDL modes. Among the
benchmark shapes, 32 change on B300 (31 dense and 1 snapshot write), 25
on B200 and 14 on GB300.

- **Token-queue persistent programs (B300):** 29 dense shapes with K 1
to 8 and M 3072 to 16384 move to token-queue (`_clc`) builds of
persistent programs. So does the M 4096 K 1 snapshot-write shape. A
token-queue build launches one CTA per token (grid M) and uses cluster
launch control. Each running CTA processes its own token and then the
tokens of the CTAs it cancels. This spreads tokens over the SMs
dynamically instead of by a static stride.
- **Token-queue persistent programs (B200):** B200 shapes also move to
token-queue builds. Examples are M 4096 K 2, which moves to
`persistent:k2_nc4_d2_f110000000000000_crfnone_clc`, and M 8192 K 6,
which moves to `persistent:k6_nc4_d2_f110000000000000_clc`.
- **Non-fast-math token-queue program (sm_103a):** B300 M 16384 K 2
moves to `persistent:k2_nc3_d2_f011010000000000_crfnone_clc`, the
non-fast-math build of a token-queue program.
- **Token-queue persistent programs (GB300, 152 SMs):** M 4096, 6144 and
8192 with K 6, 7 and 8 move to
`persistent:k6_nc4_d2_f110000000000000_clc`,
`persistent:k7_nc4_d2_f110000000000000_clc` and
`persistent:k8_nc5_d2_f110000000000000_clc`.
- **K 0 (B300 and GB300):** M 768 K 0 and M 1536 K 0 move from `k0_tma`
to `small_m_direct:k0_fm`.
- **Small M (GB300):** M 384 K 4 moves from
`persistent:k4_nc3_d2_f111000000000000_fm` to
`persistent:k4_nc3_d2_f111000000000000_fm_rcp`. M 512 K 6 moves to
`pair:k6_nc2_pbf16a_fm_cr200_pk1`, and M 512 K 8 moves to
`pair:k8_nc2_pbf16a_fm_cr200_pk1`.

The program set goes from 190 programs (222 libraries: 104 sm_100a, 118
sm_103a) to 212 programs (244 libraries: 112 sm_100a, 132 sm_103a). This
PR adds 26 libraries (10 sm_100a, 16 sm_103a) and removes 4 that no
route uses anymore: sm_100a
`persistent:k2_nc4_d2_f011000000000000_crfnone`, sm_100a
`persistent:k4_nc3_d3_f010000000000000`, sm_103a
`persistent:k4_nc3_d2_f111000000000000_fm` and sm_103a
`persistent:k5_nc4_d3_f000000000000000`. Three programs are re-homed
with identical SASS. All other libraries have SASS identical to the
previous version.

The baseline is the previous Cake version of this operator on current
main, last changed by PR #8207. All changed shapes are faster at both
PDL modes: 25 on B200 (ratios 1.011 to 1.065), 32 on B300 (1.022 to
1.108) and 14 on GB300 (1.019 to 1.126). For shapes not in the tables
below, see the timings in PRs #6980, #7014, #7338, #7374, #7411, #7453,
#7540, #7737, #8120, #8143, #8155, #8171 and #8207.

### [3d4c266](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/3d4c266d9499be1005969e089aad851466717e11)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T11:11:43Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate): non-deterministic one-cluster short backward on SM100/SM103 (#8301)

`cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate` computes `y = RMSNorm(x, w) * SiLU(z)` on BF16
rows of head dim 128. It has five variants: one forward, plus a
deterministic and a non-deterministic backward that each write the
weight gradient (dw) in BF16 or FP32.

This PR changes the non-deterministic (`deterministic=False`) backward
on sm_100a and sm_103a, for both dw dtypes and for inputs of at most 256
rows (T × H ≤ 256). On those inputs the backward now runs as one
thread-block cluster of 16 CTAs. dx and dz stay bitwise equal to the
deterministic backward. The CTAs' FP32 dw partials are added per column
in a fixed order in FP64 and rounded once. As a result, dw is the same
bits on every call and stays within the deterministic backward's error
bound, with no workspace and no atomics. The backward above 256 rows,
sm_107a and the forward do not change.

Against the previous Cake version (FlashInfer main as of #8270), the
CUDA-graph backward is 1.320-1.480x faster on B200 and 1.176-1.201x
faster on GB300. The CUDA-graph checkpointed step is 1.133-1.182x faster
on B200 and 1.043-1.104x faster on GB300. Both were faster in all 16 A/B
pairs on every served shape.

### Speedup

These bullets cover the shapes the new backward serves (T × H ≤ 256:
1x48, 2x48, 5x48, 8x32 and 13x7):

- `bwd (CUDA graph)` vs #8270: B200 1.320-1.480x, GB300 1.176-1.201x,
faster in all 16 A/B pairs.
- `bwd (CUDA graph)` vs deterministic Cake: B200 1.539-1.649x, GB300
1.597-1.628x.
- `bwd` (eager) vs deterministic Cake: B200 4.920-7.652x, GB300
10.639-14.005x. Vs best non-Cake: B200 8.800-23.081x, GB300
5.736-16.023x. The eager `bwd` span of a multi-kernel backward includes
the host launch gaps between its kernels. The A/B did not time eager
`bwd`.
- `ckpt (CUDA graph)` vs #8270: B200 1.133-1.182x, GB300 1.043-1.104x,
faster in all 16 A/B pairs.
- `ckpt (CUDA graph)` vs deterministic Cake: B200 1.329-1.388x, GB300
1.288-1.391x.
- `ckpt (CUDA graph)` vs best non-Cake: GB300 1.046-1.832x. B200 1.278x
at 5x48 and 1.410x at 8x32, but below 1x at 1x48 (0.987x), 2x48 (0.959x)
and 13x7 (0.992x).
- `ckpt (eager)` includes host time, and every ratio in these rows is
n.s.
- `fwd` runs the same code as #8270. Against #8270 it reads 0.949-1.000x
on B200 and 0.939-1.007x on GB300. All of these are n.s. except B200
13x7 (0.949x), which was slower in all 16 pairs.

Shapes above 256 rows run the same forward and backward as #8270.
Against #8270 they read 0.962-1.017x on B200 and 0.948-1.041x on GB300,
and these ratios carry no claim. Some of these rows were faster or
slower in all 16 pairs, although both arms run the same code there:

- Faster: B200 1031x48 (`fwd`, `bwd (CUDA graph)` and `ckpt (CUDA
graph)`). GB300 1031x48 `fwd`, 129x48 `bwd (CUDA graph)`, and 33x48 and
1031x48 `ckpt (CUDA graph)`.
- Slower: B200 7x48 `ckpt (CUDA graph)`. GB300 129x7 `fwd`, 33x48 and
9x32 `bwd (CUDA graph)`, and 6x48 and 129x7 `ckpt (CUDA graph)`.

A second A/B on these shapes, with fresh processes and 8 pairs per
shape, was neither consistently faster nor consistently slower on any
row.

Below 1x vs best non-Cake, on any shape:

- `fwd` on B200 at every shape (0.770-0.993x), and on GB300 at 33x48
(0.926x) and 129x48 (0.920x).
- `ckpt (CUDA graph)` on B200 at 1x48, 2x48 and 13x7 (listed above).

No ratio vs deterministic Cake is below 1x.

### How to read the tables

There is one table per GPU, with one row per shape (T × H, D = 128,
BF16, training) and operation. `ckpt` is the checkpointed step,
2×fwd+bwd.

- Shapes of at most 256 rows have five operations: `fwd`, `bwd`, `bwd
(CUDA graph)`, `ckpt (CUDA graph)` and `ckpt (eager)`.
- Larger shapes have three: `fwd`, `bwd (CUDA graph)` and `ckpt (CUDA
graph)`.

The columns give absolute µs for deterministic Cake
(`deterministic=True`), the best non-Cake implementation (named per
row), the previous Cake version (#8270, from the A/B run) and the new
path (from both runs). `vs det` and `vs non-Cake` divide by the
same-process new time. `vs #8270` is the A/B ratio, previous over new. A
ratio above 1 means the new path is faster.

- `(n.s.)` marks a ratio that is not significant:
  - `vs det`: the ratio is inside the round spread.
  - `ckpt (eager)`: every ratio.
- `vs #8270`: the new path was neither faster nor slower in all 16 A/B
pairs. A `vs #8270` ratio without the mark was faster (above 1x) or
slower (below 1x) in all 16 pairs.
- `n/a`: the non-Cake implementations have no graph-replayed backward
alone.
- `-`: the A/B run did not time that operation (`bwd`, `ckpt (eager)`).
- **changed**: the row runs the new one-cluster backward.
- `same code as #8270`: every `fwd` row, and every row of a shape above
256 rows, where both arms launch the same backward. Their ratio against
#8270 is noise and carries no claim.

### [c07e918](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c07e9181007063b152eaef946bdf1acbc05d481a)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T11:05:17Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_kda): with grad, re-copy the carried programs after the deterministic re-render (#8276) (#8292)

The deterministic package's programs were rendered again: identifiers are
renumbered, temporaries are reordered, and nine kernels drop the
NUM_MAIN_STAGES define. This package carries those programs under its own
name, byte for byte, so the 39 carried kernel units that changed are
copied again, and their 109 build.json entries (37 on sm_100a, 36 on
sm_103a, 36 on sm_107a) take the new sha256 and closure_sha256. The
build.json generator block now names the same render as the deterministic
package's. The S1 programs, the hand-off twins, the tape WY twin, the
bindings, the registry and the Python files do not change.

The deterministic package also adds the raw forget-gate records
(fwd_intra_raw, fwd_intra_v14_raw, bwd_prep_g8_raw,
bwd_prep_g8_replay_raw, bwd_prep_g8_noqg_raw, bwd_prep_g8_noqg_nokb_raw,
glm_intra_raw and param_finalize). This package refuses
use_gate_in_kernel=True, so no cell launches them and the registry does
not carry them. The registry test lists them with the deterministic
records this package does not launch and counts the deterministic
package's 75 records. The README's registry table marks them as not
shipped.

### [e39b0c7](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/e39b0c71786e3cbf8dcfc73774ba1e86b568ac2c)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-02T10:41:54Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_fused_moe): Kimi-K3 NVFP4 SiTU experts SM100 16384-token row: finalize with every routed-slot load in flight (#8289)

The Cake-generated Kimi-K3 NVFP4 SiTU expert MoE path behind
`cutlass_fused_moe(backend="cake")` uses NVFP4 weights and activations,
FP32 accumulation and BF16 output, with a single model contract (H=3584,
I=384, E=896, top_k=16). It ships 42 programs, organized as
per-token-count routes of quant, route, FC1, FC2 and finalize stages,
with seven finalize variants. This PR adds an eighth finalize variant,
`finalize:n128_q8i_mlp16`, for SM100 only. The 16384-token route
`large_q8i_p1024` uses it. It reads the same 8-bit per-tile FC2 partial
and FP32 tile scales as `finalize:n128_q8i`, with the same launch
arguments and grid. For each token, it loads all 16 routed-slot indices
and weights, then the 16 tile scales, then issues all 16 partial-row
loads before it dequantizes and accumulates in slot order. Compared with
the previous Cake version of this route, which uses `finalize:n128_q8i`,
the whole call is 1.019x faster with both uniform and skewed routing.

*Whole-call median latency for the full MoE expert layer on NVIDIA B200
(sm_100a) with CUDA 13.3.1. Baseline: the previous Cake version of the
route, measured with the same timer.*

| Tokens | Routing | Previous Cake version (us) | This PR (us) | Speedup
|
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 16384 | uniform | 1459.39 | 1432.02 | 1.019x |
| 16384 | skewed | 1384.18 | 1358.30 | 1.019x |

All other Cake variants of this kernel are unchanged: every other route,
every SM103 route, and the finalize variants `feature`, `n8`, `n16`,
`n32`, `n32_claim8`, `n128` and `n128_q8i`. The family ships on sm_100a
(B200) and sm_103a (B300).
